# CLAUDE.md archive — 2026-09-14

Everything removed from `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-09-14, in the order it appeared in the original.
Nothing was deleted. This file is NOT loaded into context automatically.

Context: `CLAUDE.md` had regrown to 1,595,201 bytes (~398,700 tokens, 5,121 lines), consuming
roughly 40% of a 1M-token context window before any work began, and making auto-compaction
impossible. This is the same failure that produced `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE.md` on 2026-08-19.

## Status snapshot (2026-09-13)

The app is under active development and substantially built. Current state:

**Most recent (2026-09-13, 1.0.37.26 through 1.0.37.30): Schedules made to be about schedules, with Life owning the things that have them.** Two reports and a design brief in one message: "When I select Schedules > Hydration it takes a good 20 seconds for it to display anything. The same happens with My Meds," and "if it is about schedules, each topic should relate to a schedule in some way... My Meds should be related to the schedule of when each med needs to be taken, and if they want to add a new med to the schedule, the link should take them to My Meds in Life where they add the specifics about the med and then tap a button to schedule it." Confirmed as the model before building: "Both prescriptions and supplements should be considered within meds... There will be maintenance schedules, hobby schedules, etc. Many schedules will be because of things contained in Life." Then "Go."

**The 20 seconds (1.0.37.26).** Hydration and My Meds were the only callers of `getDailyNutrientAnalysis`, which still walked the day one `getMealItems` query per meal and one `getFoodNutrients` query per ingredient (the sibling-fallback CTE), the pattern `getDailyNutrientBreakdown` stopped doing on 2026-08-16. The analysis is now a summary of the breakdown's own `dayTotals`, so there is one computation; the breakdown's comment about the two being "kept in sync deliberately" described a second copy that no longer exists.

**Meds (1.0.37.27).** `MyMedsLens` (about 740 lines of `schedule.tsx`) became `components/MyMedsSection.tsx` on Life, the one place a med is defined, with editing brought over from the Supplements and Prescriptions lenses and a **Schedule it** on every row that pushes `/schedule` with `openScheduleLens=meds&scheduleTreatmentId`. Schedules' Supplements, Prescriptions and My Meds lenses are replaced by one **Meds** lens: every tracked med, its reminder times, today's doses (Taken/Skip/Remove), the interaction checks, an "Add or change a med in My Meds" action band and "Edit in My Meds" per row (`/life` with `openLifeLens=myMeds&focusTreatmentId`, Life gained that param handling the same shape Schedules has). `scheduleTreatmentDose` schedules all three treatment types under their own `item_type`, so **an OTC drug gets a dose series for the first time** (`'otc'` joined the union and the interaction engine reads OTC doses). The handoff param is consumed once through a ref, per the `mealBuilderHandoff` lesson. Insights' My Meds & Interactions copy that pointed at "Schedule's own My Meds lens" corrected.

**Therapies (1.0.37.28)** moved to Signals as `components/TherapySessionsSection.tsx`: a session already happened, which is what Signals holds, and the lens's own help already sent the next visit to Appointments. Trends > Therapy Response reads the same table; its two pointers corrected. **Shopping List (1.0.37.29)** is gone from Schedules; what it showed is now a "What those days need" preview on the Grocery List's build step under Life, recomputed when the window changes. **Upkeep (1.0.37.30)** is the first schedule read from Life rather than entered: overdue, due within `DUE_SOON_DAYS`, later, and what cannot be placed yet, with Done today writing back through `markUpkeepDone` and Life's Upkeep linking to the timeline.

**Schedules now:** Meals, Today's Meals, Past Meals, Meal Plan, Hydration, Meds, Appointments, Upkeep, Exercise. `tsc` clean, `eslint` at 13 on `schedule.tsx` (down from 15; the file lost about 1,500 lines), audit 0, all 23 suites passing on every version. **Published to `preview` at Runtime version `621e8bfc...`. None of 1.0.37.27 through 1.0.37.30 confirmed on-device**, and the checks are: add a med in Life > My Meds, tap Schedule it, confirm Schedules > Meds opens with that med's reminder form and its group unfolded; set a time and confirm it appears under Today; Edit in My Meds lands back on the med expanded; log a therapy session on Signals and confirm Trends still reads it; open the Grocery List build step and confirm the preview matches what is scheduled; open Schedules > Upkeep with an Upkeep item and confirm Done today moves its date. **1.0.37.31, on instruction ("Merge the two meal generators too"):** the fixed 6-week rotation and its vegan and vegetarian tracks are gone (`lib/mealPlan.ts`, `lib/mealPlanVegan.ts`, `lib/mealPlanVegetarian.ts`, `MealPlanLens`); the dynamic generator is the one Meal Plan, key `dailyMealPlan` kept so Profile's deep link still lands. `MealPlanDay`/`MealPlanSlot` live in `lib/db.ts` and stay. **The App Guide and Walkthrough were both redeployed on 2026-09-14** (on instruction, after being held since 1.0.37.2): Schedules at nine lenses with the defined-on-Life model, Signals' real eight lenses, My Meds and Grocery List on Life, Food's lens conversions and Find a Recipe, the band look, and the one Meal Plan.

**Most recent (2026-09-13, 1.0.37.21): the band look through every Schedules lens.** "Move to Schedules. Apply the new formatting changes to all of the screens for all of the lenses for Schedules." Three scoping answers set the shape before anything was written: a list is one band per group with its rows as inset boxes; **"Everything folds"**, so every band is closed until tapped and carries its count in the title; and Food's rules carry over unchanged (a form stays open as a plain band box, an informational card folds, a menu row is an action band).

**What folds needed that Home did not.** Home remembers its sections through `homeSectionExpanded`. A per-lens copy of that would have meant a new preference per screen, so `lib/visualPreferences.ts` gained one generic `bandExpanded: Record<string, boolean>` (absence means folded, merged on update) and `hooks/useBandFolds.ts` reads and writes it: `isOpen(key)`, `toggle(key)`, keys like `schedule:meals:day` and `schedule:myMeds:Prescriptions`. A local `ScheduleBand` in `app/(tabs)/schedule.tsx` wraps `HomeSectionBand kind="fold"` with the tab colour, the count in the title and the fold state from that hook, so all thirteen lenses build the same band the same way.

**The conversion, by style rather than by hand where it could be.** `bodyContent` keeps its 16px and gains `HOME_BAND_GAP` as its column gap; `formCard`, `weekStripCard`, `hydrationSummaryCard` and the loading/error/empty notices are headerless band boxes (`homeBandStyle` with `marginHorizontal: -16`); `table` is now just the gap between rows and `row` is the inset box, so every existing list took the look with no markup change beyond the band around it. Per lens: the Meals day list, past meals, the 6-week plan as six week bands, each shopping category, today's drinks, the three My Meds groups, supplements, prescriptions, appointments, therapy sessions, and every "Things to check" and "Worth knowing" section (six of them, converted by one script) are fold bands with rows inset; Today's Meals is one band per meal with the time leading its title; "Ate out or off-plan? Say it" and "Make a Grocery List" are action bands. `DailyPlanFullReport` renders two ways, since it sits in two places: bands at the top of a one-day plan (rating box, Meals, Hydration, Nutrient coverage), inset boxes inside a day's band of a multi-day plan, where the rating dot stands in for the band's icon through `renderIcon`. No sub-screens exist on this tab, so no Back pill was needed; the Rotate modal is untouched.

**The audit learned the wrapper.** `ScheduleBand` joined `SURFACE_COMPONENTS` in `scripts/audit_bare_text_on_background.js`, and two locals in the report were renamed (`ratingBlock`, `hydrationBlock`) because the audit's usage search matched unrelated identifiers of the same name. `tsc` clean, `eslint` at the file's pre-existing 15 (verified against HEAD), audit 0, all four guards and 23 suites passing, strings confirmed in the bundle. **Published to `preview` at Runtime version `621e8bfc...`. Not yet confirmed on-device**, and this one is thirteen screens of visual judgment: open Meals, My Meds and a generated multi-day plan, fold and unfold, leave the app and come back to see the folds remembered.

**Most recent (2026-09-13, 1.0.37.14): ticks add up across meals, and the combination is shown before it is built.** 1.0.37.13 confirmed on-device as far as it went, with the correction that shaped this: "I am able to select sides from different meals, but each one says on the button Build a meal with the 1 ticked, instead of taking into account those that are ticked from other recipes. We need all that are ticked to be included, not just the one in the recipe that contains the button tapped. Then, we need to somehow show the entire meal to let the user choose to create this combination of food as a meal." The first cut kept a tick set per meal, so each meal's button counted only its own.

**One selection for the whole screen.** On Log or Schedule a Meal, `tickedDishes` is keyed by row and dish across every opened meal, each value carrying the dish's handoff item, its name and the meal it came from. A system recipe, being one dish, gets one tick for itself ("Tick to combine this dish with others into a meal"). While anything is ticked anywhere, every opened meal's button reads "Build a meal with all N ticked" and builds from all of them; with nothing ticked it takes that whole meal (or that one dish) as before. **The combination shows whole before it is built:** a "Meal you are building" band at the top of the list names every ticked dish, where it came from, an x to drop it, "Build a meal with these N dishes", and "Clear the ticks". A combination is not any of the meals it was drawn from, so it carries no name and no type, and Meal Builder asks for the type first; that identity step now names every loaded dish, so the whole plate is in view before anything is created. Meal Builder's Start from a meal you have took the identical change: ticks across meals, the same band above the list, "Use these N dishes", and each meal's own "Use all N ticked". `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, audit 0, guards and 23 suites passing, every new string confirmed in the bundle and the old per-meal "Build a meal with the N ticked" confirmed gone. **Most recent (2026-09-13, 1.0.37.9): the last four Food Stack screens are Food lenses.** "Yes, do those next too", closing what 1.0.37.7 named: `app/food-items.tsx`, `app/food-item-detail.tsx`, `app/food-product-detail.tsx` and `app/scan-product.tsx` are now `components/FoodItemsView.tsx`, `FoodItemDetailView.tsx`, `FoodProductDetailView.tsx` and `ScanProductView.tsx`, rendered inside Food's `GatedTabContent` as the lenses `myFoodsList`, `myFoodsDetail`, `myFoodProduct` and `scanProduct`. Route params became props; `router.back()` became an `onClose`/`onDone` the tab decides. The four `Stack.Screen` registrations are gone from `app/_layout.tsx`.

**How each is reached.** Scan a Product is in `FOOD_LENSES` (the corner menu), and Home's row and menu entry push `/food` with `openFoodLens=scanProduct`, handled in the focus effect beside `findMeal`. A grocery list's two Scan buttons `router.navigate` to the same, carrying `groceryListId`/`groceryItemId`; navigate rather than push because that screen sits on the Stack above the tabs. When the product is on the list, or the scan came to nothing, `returnToGroceryList` clears those params with `router.setParams` and pushes the list back on top; clearing first is what stops the pop back to Food from opening the scanner again. The three list/detail lenses have no menu entry: every one of the 24 Desktop and My Foods rows that pushed `/food-items` now calls `openMyFoodsList(params)`, which holds the list in `listParams` state; a row opens a dish or product into `detailParams`/`productParams`; a Back pill returns one level (detail to list, list to the Desktop, drilled into Saved & Favorites where that is where it lives). Edit and Use this Favorite still push `/food` with the same `editSideId`/`fromSideFavoriteId` params: a new param is what the focus effect already reacts to, so a builder opens the same way from a lens as it did from the old screen. **Most recent (2026-09-12, 1.0.36.10): Insights > Nutrients rebuilt as the first band-formatted lens outside Home, with RDA and end-of-day columns and the meals named.** Asked for directly: "the Status column is helpful but it should have 2 more columns. The first column should list the RDA of each Nutrient, and the second column should be the status of what the total amount of each nutrient will be if they eat their entire allotted meals... the names of the meals it represents... the same formatting applied to it that we just applied to the Home screen."

**At day scope the table is Nutrient | Now | RDA | End of Day.** Now is what has been logged so far with its status; End of Day is `analyzeNutrientIntake` run again over logged totals plus every still-planned meal's totals plus supplements, so it is judged by exactly the rule Now is, never a second heuristic. The planned half comes from `getProjectedNutrientTotalsByDateRange(date, date)`, which reads `status = 'planned'` only, so a scheduled meal already logged is never counted twice. The lens loads it (plus `listScheduledMealsForDate`) only when the Nutrients lens is open; `NutrientsTable` takes an optional `projected` prop so `app/food-item-detail.tsx`, which reuses the component at dish scope, needed no change. Status words in a cell are a short set (`SHORT_STATUS_LABELS`); the full sentences stay in `NUTRIENT_STATUS_LABELS` for anywhere with room.

**"Meals in This Table" is its own band above the table**: logged meal names from `breakdown.meals`, still-planned ones with their time, and a caption saying nothing is guessed for a meal not on the schedule. Both bands are `HomeSectionBand` folds in the Insights colour, in a column that cancels the lens body's 16px padding so they run edge to edge as Home's do; the table inside drops its own border and radius since the band carries them. Meal, side and item scope keep the older Amount and % of Day columns inside the same band, since RDA and End of Day mean nothing there.

**The bare-text audit learned one more shape.** The table is built into a local `const table = (...)` and placed with `{table}` inside the band, and the auditor's ancestor walk stops at the variable, so it reported 11 findings for text that is inside a surface. It now treats JSX held in a local variable the way it already treats a render helper: reported as `local:table`, cleared when every usage in that one file is covered. A first cut of that matched `styles.body` and `{ body: ... }` as usages of a local `body` and broke three previously-clean files; property names are excluded now. Verified both ways: a probe file with a bare local block still fails, and the tree is back to 0.

`tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, bare-text audit 0, all four guards clean, all twenty-two suites passing. **Not yet confirmed on-device**, and the check is the reported one: open Home's Worth a Look, confirm four columns at day scope, that End of Day moves when a meal is planned for later today, and that the meals band names what was logged and what is still to come.

**Most recent (2026-09-12, 1.0.36.8): the list behind the weekly flag count, because a chart was the wrong answer.** Reported after 1.0.36.7 landed: "The card went to 0 flags this week... A graph really doesn't seem to be the right way to go here, and if 24 were reported, there should be 24 to see."

**Both halves of that are addressed by one function.** `getFlaggedItemsByDateRange` (`lib/db.ts`) itemises every flag per day: sub-criterion, worst tier, the foods that tripped it, and the tracked conditions it is relevant to. Every existing flag count (`countFlaggedSubCriteriaByDate`, so Home, Trends and Reports) is now derived from it as the size of each day's relevant list, which is what makes the number on Home and the rows on the new `app/week-flags.tsx` screen one computation rather than two that can drift.

**The 0 is explained rather than hidden.** The 24 were the unscoped count; the scoped count for the tracked conditions on that phone is 0, most likely because whole-food meals never trip the narrow sub-criteria those conditions own. So each day also carries an "other" list: flagged, but tied to no tracked condition. Home's row names that number ("24 more flagged, not tied to a condition you track"), and the screen lists them under each day, muted, uncounted, so what stopped counting is there to see. Every row opens the tier definition, the foods, and the sub-criterion's own cited methodology through the existing `getTierDefinition`/`getSubCriterionSources`.

**What changed.** The gesture-handler ScrollView (the 2026-07-27 guess, which the 2026-08-23 report and both of today's say never worked) is replaced by the plain react-native ScrollView with `nestedScrollEnabled`, the recipe `InlineSelectList` and `KitchenSection` already use for their own nested lists. And the flip button no longer wraps the whole face: the back is a plain View whose header row, title and "Tap to flip back" line are the tap targets, with the scrolling body outside any touchable, so no JavaScript responder sits above the native scroll negotiating every drag. The front keeps its whole-face tap, since tapping anywhere to turn a card over is the point.

**If this one fails too, the next question is the one to ask before touching code again:** when dragging on the back, does the page scroll instead, or does nothing move at all? The first points at the outer page still intercepting; the second points at the touch never reaching the face (the 3D rotation's hit-testing), which is a different fix entirely. `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, bare-text audit 0. **Published to `preview` at Runtime version `621e8bfc...`. Not yet confirmed on-device.**

**Most recent (2026-09-12, 1.0.36.4): the back of a flip card could not scroll, and most likely never had.** Reported after 1.0.36.3 landed: "The flip cards look good but the backs don't seem able to scroll vertically when there is more than what can be displayed."

**The cause is Android's own nested-scroll rule, not the gesture library.** A vertical scroll view inside another vertical scroll view (a card's face, inside Home's page) hands every drag to the outer one unless the inner sets `nestedScrollEnabled`. The 2026-07-27 switch to the gesture-handler ScrollView changed which component claims the gesture and never set that flag, so the back face very likely never scrolled on a phone at all; the 2026-08-23 "cut off in mid sentence" report reads, in hindsight, as this same fault. `InlineSelectList` and `KitchenSection` already set the flag for their own nested lists, so this is the app's own precedent applied. Both faces set it now and show the scroll bar, so a face with more to read says so.

**A second real gap fixed in the same place:** the two faces are stacked, and the hidden one stays in the touch tree. Unflipped, the invisible back sat on top and would have taken a vertical drag meant for the front. Whichever face is turned away now ignores touches (`pointerEvents`), which is also what makes the front's own new scroll reachable.

**Most recent (2026-09-07, 1.0.34.61): a one-day meal plan that died on a released SQLite object, and the fan-out behind it.** Reported with the screen: "Call to function 'NativeStatement.finalizeAsync' has been rejected. Caused by: The 1st argument cannot be cast to type expo.modules.sqlite.NativeStatement (received class java.lang.Integer). Caused by: Cannot use shared object that was already released", and no plan.

**THE ERROR CLASS HAS APPEARED TWICE BEFORE AND THE OLD CAUSE IS GONE**, which is what made this worth investigating rather than retrying. 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-27 were both `getGroundThemeSync` opening a second synchronous connection to the same file, fixed at the source by reading a plain mirror file instead. Confirmed by grep this time: `lib/db.ts` is the only file that opens a database at all, there are no `closeAsync`/`closeSync` calls anywhere, and the backup he had just taken is entirely sequential. So the two-connections explanation does not apply.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS CONCURRENCY, AND THE NUMBERS ARE THE ARGUMENT.** `buildCandidatePools` mapped over every distinct curated recipe with `Promise.all`, twice: once resolving each recipe, once loading each candidate. There are **411** curated recipes and each pass is several queries deep, so a generation fired well over a thousand statements at once. **A single SQLite connection executes those one at a time regardless of how they were dispatched**, so the parallelism was never buying speed. It was buying a queue of live native statement objects and the GC churn that lets one be released underneath a pending finalize. The 2026-08-28 refetch-loop investigation saw the same error class under the same description, "dozens of overlapping calls piling onto the same SQLite connection", which is the corroboration rather than a fresh guess.

**Bounded to eight at a time** through a small `mapWithLimit`, which keeps the connection continuously busy because that is all it can be. Nothing else in the app dispatches on this scale, so this is the one site.

**AND THE RUN NO LONGER DIES OF ONE TRANSIENT FAILURE.** Generating reads and never writes, so repeating it is safe in a way retrying a write would not be. `isSharedObjectReleasedError` is now exported from `lib/db.ts` rather than copied, and both public generators retry exactly once on that specific signature. Once rather than in a loop: a second failure means something real is wrong, and saying so is more use than trying forever.

**Confirmed on-device over USB**, though stated for what it is rather than more: eight 1-day generations and three 28-day generations after the update, every one completing. The failure was intermittent, so a clean run is not proof it is gone; what can be said is that the mechanism that best explains it has been removed and a recurrence now costs a retry rather than the plan. One plausible aggravator on the day, not provable: he had just taken a backup, which reads every table in full, so the fan-out landed on a heap already under pressure.

**Most recent (2026-09-07, 1.0.34.46 through 1.0.34.60): OneDrive reached through Microsoft Graph, after the phone proved the folder picker could never get there.** Four points, given directly and quoted here because they set the bar: "1. Create a way to select a OneDrive or Google Drive folder fully selected and known to the app... 2. Use that folder to setup the mailbox for everything we need it to do for communication between partners and their children. 3. Do not deliver something as absoultely useless as you have just done. Do not tell me it is a completed solution without it being a completed solution. 4. The app must allow me to choose a shared folder, not just pretend I chose one by typing in the name of the folder."

**THE DEVICE SETTLED THE ARCHITECTURE, AND IT TOOK THREE INTENTS TO DO IT.** Fired on the real phone rather than reasoned about: `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE` does not offer OneDrive, `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` does not offer OneDrive, and `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` does. **OneDrive's storage provider hands out single files and never a folder.** So every version of "let the OS pick the folder" was dead, including the one shipped hours earlier, and Graph was the only route left. That is also why 1.0.34.42's folder picker had to be removed rather than fixed.

**AND THE CLOUD ROUTE COST NO REBUILD, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS BUILDABLE AT ALL.** `expo-web-browser`, `expo-crypto`, `expo-secure-store` and `fetch` are already compiled into both phones, so PKCE, the token store and every Graph call ship over an ordinary update. Confirmed the way this project learned to confirm it: the Runtime version printed by `eas update` stayed `621e8bfc...`, byte-identical to the installed build.

**THE PERMISSION FINDING FROM 1.0.34.41 STILL STANDS AND IS NO LONGER THE OBJECTION.** `createLink` needing `Files.ReadWrite` killed the earlier design because that design asked BOTH people to sign in to move a few hundred bytes. Reading and writing inside one folder the person picked is a different bargain: they sign in once, to their own drive, and OneDrive does the sharing.

**ONE SHARED FOLDER, AND THE APP OWNS WHAT IS INSIDE IT.** This was a correction, and the corrected shape is the right one: "The Shared Folder is Inside Story folder, not Inside Story/Mailbox. Mailbox is communications related with immediate family and partner. The Shared folder is also used for the Backup... a Shared folder is created no matter if the user is adding a partner or if they are just opening the app for the first time." So `lib/oneDriveFolders.ts` holds the one record, and `Mailbox` and `Backups` are found or made inside it rather than being two more things to set up. **Two folders to choose was one too many**, and it also let somebody point backups at the mailbox by accident, which the first version did.

**THE PICKER IS THE POINT, SO IT SHOWS THE WHOLE PATH.** Two roots (Shared with me, My files), drill down through real folders, and every screen states where it is: `OneDrive / Documents / Inside Story`. Making a folder is there too, with the limit said plainly rather than hidden: the app can make it, only OneDrive can share it. And a warning in yellow, because it is the consequence people would not guess: anything in this folder is visible to whoever it is shared with, and that includes the backups.

**TWO BUGS FOUND ON THE PHONE, BOTH INVISIBLE FROM THE CODE.** Signing in returned **AADSTS70000, the authorization code has expired**, because the redirect arrives twice, through `openAuthSessionAsync` and through the deep-link route, and both redeemed the same one-use code. Fixed by deduping on the code and sharing one promise, plus treating a refusal as success when a token is already stored. Before that, the redirect had nowhere to land at all and Android showed **Unmatched Route with the raw code printed on screen**, since no route existed at `/oauth/onedrive`.

**A STALE PATH THAT SURVIVED EVERY RELOAD**, worth naming because it looked like a caching problem and was not: the picker read the stored record once and never re-checked it, so a folder that had moved or been renamed kept reporting the old path forever. It re-resolves on open now.

**The three backups already sitting loose in the folder were moved rather than left**, through Graph, into `Backups`. Both phones were also wiped to a genuine first-run state at his instruction, which exercised the upgrade path end to end: the embedded 1.0.29.9 bundle, the migration, then 1.0.34.x over the air.

**CONFIRMED ON-DEVICE, step by step over USB:** sign-in completes, the picker lists both roots and drills down, `Use Inside Story` stores the folder, Connections reports `OneDrive / Documents / Inside Story`, Check the Folder resolves `Mailbox` under it and reports nothing waiting, and Backup & Restore reports `OneDrive / Documents / Inside Story / Backups`. The Home setup card correctly does not appear once the folder exists.

**NOT EXERCISED, and stated rather than implied:** writing a backup to OneDrive and restoring the newest one back, which needs his backup password; and a partner send and receive, which needs two phones. Lisa's phone cleared its data and is unpaired, so both signing keys are gone and pairing starts fresh.

**Most recent (2026-09-07, 1.0.34.43 through 1.0.34.45): the actual blocker found by looking at the phone, after a day spent building carriers for a problem that was already solved.** Direct instruction, after three proposals failed at the first step: "My phone is connected via USB. Look at it. See what I am seeing. I am not going to look at it until you confirm that you have actually come through."

**THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE. Three times I described what would be on screen without being able to see it, and was wrong three times.** A cloud API, a shared folder, a file exchange, each ruled out or broken at the first tap. One `adb exec-out screencap` found the real cause in two minutes. **When a device is reachable and the question is what a screen shows, look at the screen.** The standing rule against on-device walkthroughs exists to stop aimless tap-and-retap loops; it was never a reason to guess at a screen that could simply be read.

**WHAT THE SCREEN ACTUALLY SAID: "You have allowed: meals, shopping lists."** Conditions was off. `buildPartnerInvite` reads that grant and drops the codes when it is off, so showing a code again would have sent everything except the conditions. Nothing about carriers was ever the problem.

**AND THE GRANT COULD NOT BE CHANGED.** `setConnectionGrants` has been in `lib/connections.ts` since partner links shipped and **nothing in the app ever called it**. Grants were fixed at pairing, and the only way to change them was to unpair and start over, **while `app/pair.tsx` has been telling people "You can change it again, or undo it entirely, from Connections at any time."** A false claim in shipped copy, of exactly the kind 1.0.34.37 was written to remove.

**A second gate on top of it.** "Show My Code Again" was conditional on `canEncryptTo` being false, so it only appeared for pairings predating encryption. Re-showing a code is how conditions cross at all: `app/pair.tsx` rebuilds the invite from current conditions on every open, and `app/connect.tsx` applies incoming codes to a connection that already exists. **The mechanism worked and was unreachable**, which is the same shape of fault as the grant.

**THE GENERAL FAULT WORTH NAMING, since it has now appeared twice in two days.** Both of these were working code behind an unreachable control. Neither would ever surface as an error, a failed test or a type mistake, because nothing was broken; it simply could not be got at. **Checking that a feature is REACHABLE is a separate act from checking that it works**, and only the device can answer it.

**Fixed across three versions.** 1.0.34.43 matched the share call to the configuration recipe sharing already proves on a real phone (`*/*` rather than `application/octet-stream`, which messaging apps filter out of the share sheet, plus the `Share.share({ message })` call first that every other file share here already makes). 1.0.34.44 ungated the code re-exchange and corrected `PARTNER_SHARING_NOT_LIVE`, which still claimed nothing moves between two phones. 1.0.34.45 put the grant toggles on the partner row, taken verbatim from the pairing screen so one choice looks the same in both places, and made the action row wrap after **a bug I introduced the day before**: adding a fourth action pushed Remove off the right edge where it could not be reached.

**The two suite checks guarding the notice were updated rather than deleted.** They were written when nothing could travel, and now enforce the current truth: it must say conditions cross, must still say the plan does not, and must no longer claim nothing moves. **Understating what the app does teaches somebody not to trust it just as surely as overstating it.**

**CONFIRMED ON-DEVICE over USB, which is the point of this entry.** Screenshots at each step: the toggles render, ticking Conditions persists and the row changes to "You have allowed: meals, shopping lists, which conditions you track", the action row wraps onto two lines with Remove reachable, and Show My Code Again is present. **Still needs two phones**: Lisa updates, ticks the same box, then codes are shown both ways.

`tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, bare-text audit 0, all guards clean, all twenty suites passing at 1,743 checks.

**Still not built, unchanged:** carrying the generated plan between phones. Everything ruled out for it stands, and `lib/oneDriveConfig.ts` records the permission finding so it is not rediscovered: `createLink` needs `Files.ReadWrite` and `/shares` needs a bearer token, so both people would grant full access to their entire OneDrive.

**Most recent (2026-09-06, 1.0.34.42): the carrier settled, after three were ruled out on evidence in one day.** Reported directly, on a real device: "Pick a shared folder only opens the phone folder structure and doesn't open the ability to go to onedrive," then, when asked to check the picker's drawer, "there is no menu like you're talking about."

**THE FULL LIST OF WHAT WAS RULED OUT, AND WHY EACH ONE DIED. Worth keeping in this much detail, because every one of them looks obviously right until it is checked, and each was killed by one specific documented fact rather than by taste.**

1. **LAN sync.** `@dr.pogodin/react-native-static-server` compiles lighttpd and pcre2 from C through CMake and its own README says Expo is "not supported officially"; installing it moved the fingerprint, so it is a rebuild plus a reinstall on both phones before a line of it runs. `react-native-tcp-socket` is an old-architecture bridge module, and Expo requires the New Architecture from SDK 55, so it is a dead end with a deadline. Also only ever works on one network.
2. **A cloud API.** A Microsoft Entra app registration was completed end to end (multitenant plus personal accounts, native redirect on the scheme this app already owns, client id live in `lib/oneDriveConfig.ts`) and then abandoned on two findings. **Graph's `createLink` needs `Files.ReadWrite` for a personal account**, not `Files.ReadWrite.AppFolder`, meaning full read and write to somebody's entire OneDrive to make the share link. And **`/shares` requires a bearer token**, with the docs stating plainly that the Shares API cannot be used to reach anonymously shared content without a user context. So the whole premise, sender authenticates and the reader just fetches, is false: BOTH people sign in and BOTH grant access to every document and photo they own, to move a few hundred bytes.
3. **A shared folder through the OS picker.** Confirmed on a real device rather than reasoned about: **OneDrive does not appear in the Android folder picker at all**, and there is no drawer to find it in. CommonsWare's Scoped Storage Stories says few cloud providers support `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE`, and Android's own docs confirm folder selection is each provider's choice. **The fallback offered alongside it was also wrong and should have been checked first: OneDrive for Android keeps no locally synced folder**, unlike the Windows client, so there was nothing local to point at either.
4. **A QR code for the payload.** Measured, not guessed: condition codes fit easily, a one-week plan is borderline at 141x141 modules, and anything longer will not fit. Dictionary-packing the ids made it BIGGER, against instinct.

**WHAT SHIPPED IS THE ONE CHANNEL THIS APP OWNS END TO END: the person hands the file over themselves.** `sendToPartnerAsFile` seals the payload, writes a `.is` file and opens the share sheet; `importPartnerFile` opens the OS file browser and reads one back. No account, no scope, no permission from any provider, works when the two people are apart, and works for children with no new mechanism.

**BOTH HALVES WERE ALREADY BUILT AND PROVEN HERE, so this is wiring rather than new capability.** `writeRawIsFile` has written `.is` files since recipe sharing; `shareFileIfAvailable` is the second of the two native calls Android has always needed (React Native's own `Share.share` silently discards its `url` field there); and `File.pickFileAsync` is what Backup & Restore already uses. Nothing new was installed and the fingerprint did not move.

**PICKING RATHER THAN TAPPING IS THE WHOLE TRICK, and it retires a limitation this project has carried since 1.0.34.34.** Tapping a received `.is` file has never reliably opened this app on Android, because a `content://` URI handed over by another app usually carries no filename for the intent filter to match, which needs a native rebuild to address and might still fail on the next sending app. Opening the file browser from INSIDE the app sidesteps all of it: no intent filter, no OS registration, nothing outside this app has to cooperate. **That is the same criterion that chose QR pairing over a pasted code, applied to the payload instead of the invite.**

**The four checks are unchanged and deliberately reuse the same functions rather than a second copy**, because a carrier changing must not change what has to be true before anything is stored: addressed to this device, opens with this device's key, the fingerprint INSIDE the sealed payload matches the one outside it, and that fingerprint belongs to somebody paired as a partner.

**The shared folder is kept rather than deleted, and demoted rather than hidden.** Where a storage app does support folder selection, or on an SD card or anything doing real local folder sync, it is the same exchange without the sending step. The card says plainly that most cloud apps on Android do not offer it and names OneDrive as one of them, rather than leaving somebody to discover an empty picker the way this was discovered.

**Two reversals in one feature, both from investigating rather than assuming, and both stated at the time.** LAN to cloud, then folder to file. The registration is the part that survives: it is what iOS may still need, and `lib/oneDriveConfig.ts` records the exact permission finding so nobody rediscovers it.

`tsc` clean, `eslint` clean on every touched file, bare-text audit 0, all guards clean, all twenty suites passing at 1,742 checks. No fingerprint input touched. **Not yet confirmed on-device**, and the check is the reported one end to end: Send Mine to Them on one phone, Get What They Sent on the other, then confirm a generated plan says it covers both people.

**Named and not built:** carrying the generated plan itself, which needs resolving each scheduled meal through its carrier favorite to the curated recipe ids underneath; automatic background exchange, which every remaining option makes expensive; and LAN sync, still deferred.

**Most recent (2026-09-06, 1.0.34.41): the carrier, and the cloud API route ruled out by evidence after being built as far as a live registration.** Asked to walk through the OneDrive registration, which was done: a real Entra app exists, multitenant plus personal accounts, native redirect on the scheme this app already owns, client id live in `lib/oneDriveConfig.ts`.

**THEN THE PERMISSION CHECK KILLED IT, AND CHECKING BEFORE BUILDING IS THE ONLY REASON THAT WAS CHEAP.** Graph's `createLink` permissions table lists, for a personal Microsoft account, least-privileged **`Files.ReadWrite`**. `Files.ReadWrite.AppFolder` is not accepted at all. The share link is what the whole design rested on (sender authenticates, receiver just fetches, no account needed on the reading side), so the narrow scope cannot deliver it. The real price of the cloud route is therefore **full read and write access to somebody's entire OneDrive, every document and photo, to move a few hundred bytes**, and the consent screen says exactly that to whoever is being asked. Disproportionate, and the kind of screen people back out of.

**WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD IS THE PERSON'S OWN ORIGINAL DESIGN, and it was dismissed too early the first time.** Their words were "I thought we were just going to share a OneDrive directory". Android and iOS both expose a folder picker through `Directory.pickDirectoryAsync`, part of expo-file-system's SDK 54 class API, and **expo-file-system is already linked into the shipped build**. So: the person picks one folder, this app gets persistent read and write inside that folder and visibility of nothing else, and whatever already syncs it moves the bytes. **No registration, no scope, no OAuth, no provider lock-in, and no rebuild.** Verified against the real type declarations and against both the native Kotlin and Swift sources before a line was written, rather than trusted from documentation.

**Four files, split so the risky half is testable.** `lib/syncInbox.ts` is pure naming and addressing; `lib/syncInboxStorage.ts` does the picker, the persisted URI and the reads and writes; `lib/partnerTransfer.ts` sequences payload, sealing, addressing and storage without re-deciding any of them; the Connections card is the one place it is reachable. Same pure/storage split `groceryList.ts` and `groceryDb.ts` already use.

**AN INBOX PER RECIPIENT, WHICH DELETES THE LOCKING PROBLEM RATHER THAN SOLVING IT.** One file per direction, named `is-sync-{to}-{from}.json`, overwritten on each send. Two devices sharing one file over a service that reconciles whenever it feels like it is not a problem worth building a lock on top of. It also extends to children with no new mechanism: a third device is just more filenames in the same folder.

**THE FOLDER IS ASSUMED VISIBLE TO THE WHOLE HOUSEHOLD, AND THAT IS FINE.** Every payload is sealed to one recipient by `lib/partnerCrypto.ts` before it reaches the folder, so a listing reveals who is talking to whom and nothing about what was said.

**FOUR THINGS MUST AGREE BEFORE ANYTHING IS STORED**, each checked rather than inferred from the one before: the file is addressed to this device, the sealed box opens with this device's key, the fingerprint INSIDE the payload matches the one in the filename, and that fingerprint belongs to somebody actually paired as a partner. **A filename is not evidence**, which is what `resolveSender` exists for: a mismatch is refused rather than attributed to the wrong person.

**ONE UNREADABLE FILE DOES NOT SINK THE READ.** A synced folder routinely holds a file still arriving, and refusing the whole inbox over one half-written entry would mean a plan never lands on a busy day. Each failure is skipped and counted so the count can be reported rather than the folder called empty.

**THE FIFTH OCCURRENCE OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN WORST TESTING TRAP, caught by mutation testing rather than by reading.** Dropping the `.json` requirement from `parseSyncFileName` broke nothing: the `.tmp` fixture was being rejected by the slice arithmetic, not by the extension rule, so two rules agreed and neither was tested. The case that isolates it is a **five-character** extension, where removing five characters lands exactly on a valid pair. `.part` is what several downloaders name a file mid-arrival, so this was a real gap, not a contrived one. Three checks added; all six mutations then caught.

**Real synced-folder debris is tested rather than imagined**, since this is where the app meets somebody's actual storage: OneDrive conflict copies, Dropbox conflicted-copy naming, numbered duplicates, partial downloads, SAF `content://` URIs with percent-encoded document ids, posix and Windows paths, and case-folded names (FAT32 folds case, so a returned name may not be the one written).

**What crosses today is condition codes, and that is the loop the person originally asked to close** ("the two sides need to be able to combine the conditions for each user into one meal system that both users see"): received codes go through `setPartnerConditionCodes`, and `lib/partnerPlanning.ts` already plans around both people once they are there. **The generated plan does not cross yet**, because that needs resolving each scheduled meal through its carrier favorite to the curated recipe ids underneath. The payload field and its tests already exist, so it is a wiring gap, and it is **named on the card itself** rather than left as a silent omission.
