## Removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23

CLAUDE.md had reached 113,010 characters, past the ~100 KB ceiling it sets for itself. Each passage below was cut or condensed there and is kept here verbatim, in the order it appeared in the file. The standing rule in each case stays in CLAUDE.md; what was removed is the build account, the bug history and the enumerations behind it.

### CLAUDE.md lines 52

The 1.0.49.6 build account under "When a supplement is taken belongs to scheduling" in ## What this app is. The principle stays in CLAUDE.md; this is the implementation detail removed from it.

**When a supplement is taken belongs to scheduling, and it matters.** Same statement: supplements carry rules about with or without food, with water or with fat, not with certain foods, and not with other vitamins, minerals, acids and hormones they compete with, synergistic and antagonistic both. Those rules live in the interaction-rules engine and the dose timeline in Schedules > Meds. Built 1.0.49.6: Schedules > Today's Meals is the day itself, meals and doses interleaved by the clock, and an opened dose reads the meals around it. `lib/interactionRules.ts` only ever checked a dose time against another DOSE time, and checked fat against the WHOLE day, so levothyroxine at 7:00 beside a yogurt breakfast at 7:30 passed silently while a calcium capsule at 7:30 was warned about. `lib/doseMealTiming.ts` closes that: it takes the six `timing_separation` rules and the five checkable `dietary_cofactor` rules with `subject_b = fat_total`, finds the closest meal that qualifies inside the separation window, and says which meal, how much of what it carries, and how far apart the two are. `MEAL_AMOUNT_THAT_MATTERS` in that file is a set of working thresholds, NOT doses from a trial (no source states the amount at which an ordinary meal starts to compete), which is why every sentence it generates names the real amount rather than asking to be trusted. A meal with nothing resolvable to the food database is `nutrientsResolved: false` and reads as could not be checked, never as carrying nothing. `getDayMealAndDoseTimeline` in `lib/db.ts` assembles the day (one ingredient-resolution cache across it) and the module has no database and no React in it, so `scripts/test_dose_meal_timing.js` (68 checks) covers the wording without a phone. Nothing on that lens writes: times, taken, skipped and removed stay on Meds, so one place holds that record. Leaving supplements out of a single meal's nutrient arithmetic (Insights counts them at Whole Day scope only) is about arithmetic and says nothing about timing.

### CLAUDE.md lines 106

The full "No text on a tab background" standing rule, ## Standing rules. Condensed in CLAUDE.md; the rule, the three remedies and both audit scripts survive there.

- **No text ever sits directly on a tab's photographic background without a surface of its own.** Direct instruction, 2026-08-29: "No font should ever be directly on the tab background without its own background anywhere in the app. I don't know all of the places where that exists right now, but it is throughout the Insights area. Some of them are headers that should just be a part of the informational box it represents." Three remedies, in order of preference: (1) a heading that labels ONE card moves INSIDE that card as its first row (`tableHeading` in `insights.tsx`, `myMedsGroupHeading` in `schedule.tsx`), which is what "Needs attention today" needed; (2) a heading introducing a GROUP of separate cards, or a standalone empty/error/loading/footnote line, gets a surface of its own (`groupHeadingChip`/`panelStandalone`, defined per screen); (3) an outline-only control (a bordered button or pill with no fill) gets a fill, since its label is otherwise sitting on the photo. Prefer giving the surface to the shared CONTAINER (a field row, a stat group, a heading-plus-subheading pair) over chipping each line, so related text reads as one block rather than several stacked boxes. `scripts/audit_bare_text_on_background.js` is the check: it walks the real TypeScript AST, climbs each Text element's JSX ancestors, and resolves render helpers and components ACROSS files, so a chart component whose labels are bare in its own file is correctly cleared when every screen that renders it puts it inside a card. It reported 449 findings across 43 files when written and must stay at 0; run it before calling any UI work done. **Its companion since 2026-09-21 is `scripts/audit_dark_text_shadow.js`**, after "any font that is black ... looks like a smudged font" on both the phone and Windows: it folds every StyleSheet entry and every Text-like element's style array (arrays, `&&`, ternaries, `colors.X` tokens resolved to a luminance) and reports dark text carrying a shadow, which the 2026-08-29 hand sweep had no guard for; it found 31 when written and must stay at 0, and a dark colour on a shadowed shared style is overridden with `textShadowColor: 'transparent', textShadowRadius: 0` rather than by splitting the style. Two supporting scripts exist for applying fixes at scale: `scripts/add_style_background.js` (add a fill to a named StyleSheet entry across many files, for a control copy-pasted across all eleven builders) and `scripts/wrap_bare_text_lines.js` (add a style to specific reported lines, needed because the same style name is often used both inside cards and outside them in one file, so a global find/replace would nest surfaces).

### CLAUDE.md lines 117

The full "Lists are open-ended, and removing an entry never orphans" standing rule, ## Standing rules. Condensed in CLAUDE.md; both halves of the rule, the module names and the alphabetical-chooser rule survive there.

- **Lists are open-ended, and removing an entry never orphans or destroys a record.** Direct instruction, 2026-09-20: "This app will collect the details of a person's life, but we need to make it as future-proof as possible by giving ways to add things in lists that we haven't foreseen the need for, or the existence of," and, on removal, "I don't think anything should be orphaned if the user deletes a field label they created. That isn't good database management." Two halves. (1) Any picker over a fixed list of kinds, spaces, categories or labels gets an "Add a ... of your own" entry backed by its own table (`garden_cost_kinds`, `garden_spaces` are the precedents, shared `GardenSpaceField` and the Kind picker in `GrowingCostsLens` the shape: sentinel option, one-line form in place, Rename and Remove for the person's entries only, dedupe by lowercased name). (2) Removing an entry that records read: things in use are moved to a replacement the person picks first (the form in place says how many and waits for the pick; Remove goes through only then), things with history are retired rather than deleted and stay readable as documentation (`garden_spaces.retired_at`), and a row is deleted outright only when nothing refers to it. Never fall back to a catch-all like Something else, never NULL a column, never cascade. The same applies to the things themselves: a garden area with anything recorded under it moves to Past Areas (`archived_at`), only once every grow in it has finished, and Delete is offered only while nothing is recorded under it (`deleteGardenPlot` refuses otherwise). Decision logic lives in pure modules (`planSpaceRemoval` in `lib/gardenSpaces.ts`, `pastAreaBlocker` in `lib/gardenAreaLifecycle.ts`) so `scripts/test_garden_spaces.js` and `scripts/test_garden_area_lifecycle.js` cover it without a phone. Since 2026-09-21 a new open list needs no table of its own: `garden_custom_terms` holds any list keyed by name (`equipment_kind`, `light_type`, `light_spectrum`, `container_material` so far; the spectrum list joined 2026-09-21 by direct request, "Spectrum of light also needs to have the ability to create a new user editable entry"), `components/GardenTermField.tsx` is the picker with the add, rename and move-first removal built in, and `planTermRemoval` in `lib/growSetup.ts` carries the decision. **Chooser lists of names read alphabetically** (direct instruction, 2026-09-21: "Make sure that the chooser lists are listed in alphabetical order"): `sortByLabel` in `lib/choiceOrder.ts` sorts by label, case-insensitively, with the person's entries merged in among the built-ins rather than appended, a fixed entry (Unassigned, Something else, the add-your-own sentinel) held at its end by the caller, and a list that is a scale (sunlight, plant stage, planting status, moisture, cadence, units) left in its natural order. Applied on Garden so far: equipment kinds, light types, container materials, spaces, growing-cost kinds, area and cost-group pickers, compost pile kinds, material suggestions and classes, light spectrum, the Greenhouse/Indoor/Outdoor choice, and the country list (which `constants/countries.ts` keeps in code order). Build a new name list through it; the tests in `scripts/test_grow_setup.js`, `test_garden_spaces.js` and `test_garden_money.js` assert the order.

The phone signs in to Microsoft Graph because Android will not let an app pick a OneDrive folder; that sign-in ends at a `hashimotosapp://` redirect nothing on a PC is registered for, so it waited for a result that could never come. `lib/oneDriveAuth.ts` reports signed in on desktop and `lib/oneDriveGraph.ts` sends every one of its calls to `lib/desktop/cloudFolder.ts`, which addresses a folder as `driveId 'disk'` with the absolute path as its `itemId` in the same `app_meta` row, so nothing in `lib/db.ts`, `lib/syncInbox.ts` or the backup code changed. `desktop/cloudFolder.js` does the file work in the main process: roots from `OneDriveConsumer`, `OneDrive` and `OneDriveCommercial`, a write landing as a temp file then a rename so the OneDrive client never uploads a half-written backup, and writes refused outside a detected root, the home folder, or a folder picked through the OS dialog this run. A folder travels between the two kinds of device by its sentence, "OneDrive / Apps / Inside Story", mapped back onto the disk by `folderFromPhonePath` and onto Graph by `folderFromComputerPath`.

A phone holding a folder chosen on a computer adopts it by its sentence (`folderFromComputerPath`), and a folder that cannot be reached is said once per run.
    2. **Every arrival is a three-way merge, record by record** (`lib/snapshotMerge.ts`, which imports nothing): base, here and there, decided per row, so a row only one side touched carries straight over and a row both sides touched is settled by the time the row itself carries (`TIME_COLUMNS`), falling back to whichever device saved later. The later change stands and the other is written down as a clash rather than vanishing. The agreed copy is the third thing a merge needs, kept as a plain `inside-story-sync-base.json` at `Paths.document`; missing but clean means what is here IS the agreed copy. **That copy is what the OTHER device last sent, never what this one last published** (1.0.49.11, and the same correction to `peer_sync_base` in `lib/peerSyncDevice.ts`, which had written its base from the merged result). A save learns nothing about the other device: it puts a file in the folder and cannot know whether anybody has read it. Writing the base from a save claimed the other device had seen those rows, so when that device saved a copy it had built before reading ours, every row added here read as a row deleted there and was dropped (`mergeOneTable`'s `theyMoved` branch), which flipped a row between present and absent on each exchange and could lose a change made inside the minute OneDrive takes to carry a file. So the base moves only when a copy is read: a load takes it whole, a merge takes what arrived, and a save calls `seedMergeBase`, which writes only when there is no base at all. `mergeTables` returns that arriving copy as `incoming`, renumbered into this device's ids, because the base has to be in the id space of the device holding it (`renumberIncoming`, `scanned_products`). It goes stale in the safe direction: the other device has usually merged past the copy recorded here, which makes a row it holds read as added rather than deleted, and an addition is kept. Sync Now never forces, since forcing would put this device's rows where both devices' rows belong, and `planBeforeSave` looks for a copy to take in BEFORE checking whether anything here is unsaved. **A merge marks the device unsaved only when it has something to send** (1.0.49.10, reported as the Windows app restarting about once a minute, which was the window reloading after a merge): `mergeTables` returns `sendsBack`, comparing each table's merged rows against the rows that arrived regardless of the order they were read back in, and `mergeSnapshot` sets `dirtySince` from it. While every merge marked the device unsaved, the save that followed uploaded a copy even when the merge had taken in everything, the other device read that fresh record as an arrival, merged, saved in its turn, and two devices left open answered each other every half minute.     3. **What changed is said in words, and the words carry no health content out of the encryption.** `lib/snapshotChanges.ts` reduces the stripped tables to one `{n, h}` per table and diffs two stamps into phrases through a map of roughly 50 areas ("3 more meals and edits to your schedule. Not saved here yet: 1 more capture"), where a count comes from one table per area so a salad and its six ingredient rows read as "1 more salad", four phrases at most, then "N other things". **The list rides INSIDE the encrypted snapshot** (a `syncChanges` key), never in the plaintext record, since what somebody added to is as much their health as what they added; the baseline it is diffed against is too big for the Android secure store and lives in `app_meta`, written with the write tracking suspended.
    4. **There is a log either way.** `sync_change_log` plus `lib/syncLog.ts`, read on `app/sync-activity.tsx` and reached from Profile > Backup & Restore, one band per merge with each line naming who did it and marking a clash, grouped so a shopping list with eleven items ticked off is one line. **Nothing is said out loud any more, and the log is where a merge is read.** Direct instruction, 1.0.49.9: "we have proven the changes work and are reliable. Now we need to turn off the notifications until we see a reason to make them available, how and where." `ANNOUNCE_MERGES` in `lib/snapshotSync.ts` is a constant set to false, read by `lib/snapshotSyncDevice.ts` and `lib/peerSyncDevice.ts`, so one line covers both kinds of merge, and turning the notices back on is that one line. It is a constant rather than a changed default because `readSyncState` merges stored settings over `EMPTY_SYNC_STATE` and both devices already carry `announce: true`, so a flipped default would have left them talking; the per-device switch in Profile is gone rather than sitting there turned off, since where to offer it again is the open question. Three things still speak: the first-time question, which is why `lib/snapshotChanges.ts` and its tests stay; a folder that cannot be reached, since a sync failing in silence was the 1.0.42.30 bug; and "Save to the Shared Folder Now", which was pressed on purpose. The notice paths are left standing rather than deleted. Covered by `scripts/test_snapshot_merge.js` (178), `test_snapshot_sync.js` (87), `test_snapshot_changes.js` (101) and `test_sync_log.js` (25).

### CLAUDE.md lines 148

The Delivery bullet, ## Technology stack. The rule survives in CLAUDE.md; the per-build inventory of 1.0.37.33, .41 and .42 and the dated "wired up as of" list are the part kept only here.

- **Delivery: JS ships OTA, native ships by rebuild.** `eas update --branch preview` publishes every JS change and is the last step of every request. **Publish it as `eas update --branch preview --platform android`, never with the platform left off.** Without a platform eas-cli exports all three, and the web export fails on `expo-sqlite`'s `wa-sqlite.wasm` because web only resolves through the desktop stand-ins under `INSIDE_STORY_DESKTOP=1` (`metro.config.js`); the desktop app ships as an installer rather than as an OTA bundle, so nothing consumes a web update anyway, and a JS change reaches Windows only through `node desktop/build-web.js` plus `cd desktop && npm run dist` (see the desktop section’s installer check). `eas build --profile preview --platform android` (via `npx --yes eas-cli`, no local install) is only for changes to native code, and forces both phones to reinstall. `runtimeVersion` is a fingerprint; `fingerprint.config.js` skips app.json versions and `.gitignore` so neither drifts the runtime (each was found stranding OTA updates, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-14). Before any rebuild, gather everything rebuild-gated into it. It was not: `LensHub` at Normal spacing already wanted 402 dp against a 411 dp landscape phone. `useWindowDimensions()` reports dp rather than pixels, so **one measurement covers every case at once**, and there are four of them: Android's **Display size** setting (which raises the density, so the same screen reports 1.1x to 1.3x fewer dp, and which needs no second device and no rotation, making it the one most people will actually hit), a **landscape or split-screen viewport**, a **foldable**, and an **Android 16+ large screen**, which ignores an app's orientation lock outright. `app.json` sets `"orientation": "portrait"`, so an ordinary phone will not rotate; that narrows who sees the short viewport, and does not remove it, since `"supportsTablet": true` is set too.
  - The arithmetic lives in `lib/menuFit.ts` (`menuCardRoom`, `fitMenuCard`), pure and with no React in it, so `node scripts/test_menuFit.js` can check it without a phone. `useMenuCardFit(desired, minHeight)` in `constants/floatingButton.ts` is the hook every menu calls: that file already owns where each hub sits, so how much room that position leaves belongs there too rather than being hand-copied into each hub.
  - **A clamped card scrolls.** All three menus put their content through a `ScrollView` unconditionally, because a `ScrollView` whose content is shorter than its frame simply does not scroll, so there is one code path to be right about rather than two. `TabHub`'s card split into a fixed-height `cardFrame` (surface, rounded corners, clip) and a scrolling `card` grid to do it.
  - `node scripts/audit_menu_card_fit.js` is the check and must stay at 0. It requires every menu file to call `useMenuCardFit`, and rejects a hand-typed `height`, `maxHeight` or `minHeight` on any `card*` style in one, which is how `MyItemsHub` came to carry a flat `maxHeight: 320` with a second flat `maxHeight: 260` inside it that had to be kept exactly 60 less. Both are gone. Run it beside `audit_chrome_font_scale.js` and `audit_bare_text_on_background.js`.
  - `PageIdentityLabel` was checked and deliberately not changed: it is 78 dp tall, pinned to the bottom edge, and asks for about 92 dp of window, so a window losing height takes nothing from it. The menus overflowed because they are tall and grow upward.

### CLAUDE.md lines 171-178 (second pass)

The designed multi-device sync model (locking, active takeover, stale-lock expiration) and the last-write-wins note under it, ## Architecture decisions. Superseded in practice by the shared-folder three-way merge that shipped from 1.0.42.28; CLAUDE.md now carries a summary and points here.

**Multi-device sync model:** the encrypted cloud snapshot is the current state, not just a backup. A device pulls it, decrypts locally, works fully offline against it, and pushes an updated snapshot back. Three layered safety mechanisms prevent concurrent edits:

1. *Locking.* The first device to pull holds exclusive control, recorded in cloud metadata. Control persists until the app closes, the screen locks, or an inactivity timer fires.
2. *Active takeover.* A second device sends a **visible, tap-required** push to the controlling device, deliberately not a silent push, which iOS and Android throttle unreliably. If unanswered in 1 to 2 minutes, the requester is offered "take control anyway," shown exactly how stale the other device's last save was.
3. *Stale-lock expiration.* A hard 30-minute maximum lease, so an unreachable device can never permanently lock someone out.

Underneath all three: last-write-wins plus a visible activity log. Deliberately not a CRDT system, a choice validated by AnkiWeb's own mature sync falling back to one-way overwrite when changes can't merge.


### CLAUDE.md lines 190-200 (second pass)

The seven-step ordered prerequisite list for the security work, given 2026-08-15, plus the 2026-09-06 note on which steps turned out to be built. ## Architecture decisions. CLAUDE.md now carries the status of each step without the per-step reasoning.

**Ordered prerequisite list for the security work** (given directly 2026-08-15, so it survives across sessions):

1. **Pick a cryptography library.** `expo-crypto` only does hashing and secure random bytes. The well-precedented choice is NaCl-based (`react-native-libsodium` or `tweetnacl-js`) for Ed25519 signing, X25519 exchange, and XSalsa20-Poly1305. Make this an explicit decision, since it affects bundle size and whether a native rebuild is needed.
2. **Per-device identity.** A keypair generated once on first use, private key in `expo-secure-store` (Android Keystore, iOS Keychain), never plain SQLite or AsyncStorage. Buildable and testable standalone.
3. **Local Connections table.** Name, other person's public key, pairing date. Testable with seeded data.
4. **The invitation and pairing exchange**, the biggest and most novel piece. Two devices with no server need an out-of-band public-key swap with explicit accept on both sides. A QR code deserves direct consideration: it's the pattern Signal and WhatsApp use for device linking, and Expo already bundles camera and barcode scanning.
5. **Sign (and optionally encrypt) the existing envelope shape.** `ShareEnvelope`, `encodeEnvelope`, and `decodeShareEnvelope` in `lib/sharing.ts` already define the payload. Add signature verification against the stored public key, rejecting outright on mismatch.
6. **`.is` OS-level file-type registration, deliberately last.** Android intent-filter and iOS document-type changes in `app.json` via a config plugin, plus a native rebuild. It's only a different delivery mechanism for the same signed envelope, so doing it first would burn a rebuild cycle on a payload shape that may still change.
7. **Extend beyond recipes** to gardening, exercise, and so on. Mechanical once 1 through 6 exist.

**Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are in fact built, confirmed by reading the code on 2026-09-06: this list saying otherwise was stale.** `tweetnacl` is a dependency, `lib/deviceIdentity.ts` keeps a private key in `expo-secure-store`, `connections` stores a unique public key per person, and `decodeShareEnvelope` verifies every received payload against the verbatim signed bytes. Step 4 (the pairing exchange) was one-sided and became genuinely two-way in 1.0.34.30. Step 6 (`.is` OS registration) is in `app.json`'s intent filters (content:// and file:// `.is` paths, plus the https App Link added 2026-09-14). Step 7 (extending past recipes) is still open, alongside transport. The rest should be designed and built *together with* real tier-separation work, not as a separate phase beforehand.

27. **External data program: nine public-data lookup projects behind one Cloudflare Worker.** Brainstormed and written up 2026-09-14 into the [Project Tracker](https://app.notion.com/p/c9597dcb8a1d4cc5bc34ef87a4a097df) as nine Deferred "Coming project" rows plus one Decision row, [External lookups: three privacy shapes, one Worker](https://app.notion.com/p/3db53652f272816d8051f1d335574853). Nothing is built. This is accepted scope rather than a loose idea, so read those rows before re-deriving any of it. The rule settled first, which every outside request follows: (1) a keyed lookup, a barcode or product name in and a label out, routed through the `inside-story-site` Worker off a D1 snapshot with the edge cache in front, so only the key leaves the phone; (2) anything keyed by condition, which the Worker pre-fetches for all 19 on a schedule and the phone downloads as a whole bundle, so a device never makes a per-condition request; (3) anything keyed by location, coarsened to a rounded coordinate or a city and never the precise fix, stated in-product the way the voice boundary is stated, and opt-in. The nine projects: supplement labels by barcode (DSLD), packaged foods (USDA Branded Foods plus Open Food Facts, which also moves `lib/barcodeLookup.ts`'s direct calls and its bundled USDA API key behind the Worker), OTC medicines by barcode and prescriptions by name (openFDA, RxNorm), recall matching against what a person scanned or saved (openFDA enforcement, FSIS), weather, barometric pressure, UV and air quality in Pattern Finder (Open-Meteo), current clinical trials per condition (ClinicalTrials.gov), the stated reference-database gaps as unified-pipeline adapters (Fineli, BEDCA, the Nordic tables), garden, soil and Earth Matters data (USDA Hardiness Zone, PLANTS, NRCS Soil Data Access, PDP, Total Diet Study, fish mercury), and a PubMed citation-verification script for every Digest reference. Agreed order: recalls and weather first, then supplement and OTC barcode work together. Cost baseline is Workers Paid at $5/month from the day the first lookup ships, with monthly snapshot refreshes run by a GitHub Actions cron loading into fresh tables and swapping by rename. One product rule carried over: when a refresh brings a newer record for something already saved, the app offers it on next open and never silently replaces what the person confirmed.

- **Lists are open-ended, and removing an entry never orphans or destroys a record.** Direct instruction, 2026-09-20: "This app will collect the details of a person's life, but we need to make it as future-proof as possible by giving ways to add things in lists that we haven't foreseen the need for, or the existence of," and, on removal, "I don't think anything should be orphaned if the user deletes a field label they created. That isn't good database management." Two halves. (1) Any picker over a fixed list of kinds, spaces, categories or labels gets an "Add a ... of your own" entry: a sentinel option, a one-line form in place, Rename and Remove for the person's entries only, dedupe by lowercased name. A new open list needs no table of its own, since `garden_custom_terms` holds any list keyed by name and `components/GardenTermField.tsx` is the picker with the add, rename and move-first removal built in; `garden_cost_kinds` and `garden_spaces` (shared `GardenSpaceField`) are the older per-table precedents. (2) Removing an entry that records read: things in use are moved to a replacement the person picks first (the form in place says how many and waits for the pick), things with history are retired rather than deleted and stay readable as documentation (`garden_spaces.retired_at`), and a row is deleted outright only when nothing refers to it. Never fall back to a catch-all like Something else, never NULL a column, never cascade. The same applies to the things themselves: a garden area with anything recorded under it moves to Past Areas (`archived_at`) only once every grow in it has finished, and `deleteGardenPlot` refuses to delete while anything is recorded under it. Decision logic lives in pure modules (`planSpaceRemoval` in `lib/gardenSpaces.ts`, `pastAreaBlocker` in `lib/gardenAreaLifecycle.ts`, `planTermRemoval` in `lib/growSetup.ts`) so the test scripts cover it without a phone. **Chooser lists of names read alphabetically** (direct instruction, 2026-09-21): `sortByLabel` in `lib/choiceOrder.ts` sorts by label, case-insensitively, with the person's entries merged in among the built-ins rather than appended, a fixed entry (Unassigned, Something else, the add-your-own sentinel) held at its end by the caller, and a list that is a scale left in its natural order. Build a new name list through it.

- **Delivery: JS ships OTA, native ships by rebuild.** `eas update --branch preview` publishes every JS change and is the last step of every request. **Publish it as `eas update --branch preview --platform android`, never with the platform left off.** Without a platform eas-cli exports all three, and the web export fails on `expo-sqlite`'s `wa-sqlite.wasm` because web only resolves through the desktop stand-ins under `INSIDE_STORY_DESKTOP=1` (`metro.config.js`); the desktop app ships as an installer rather than as an OTA bundle, so nothing consumes a web update anyway, and a JS change reaches Windows only through `node desktop/build-web.js` plus `cd desktop && npm run dist` (see the desktop section's installer check). `eas build --profile preview --platform android` (via `npx --yes eas-cli`, no local install) is only for changes to native code, and forces both phones to reinstall. **Before any rebuild, gather everything rebuild-gated into it.** `runtimeVersion` is a fingerprint; `fingerprint.config.js` skips app.json versions and `.gitignore` so neither drifts the runtime (each was found stranding OTA updates, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-14). The per-build inventory of what each of 1.0.37.33, 1.0.37.41 and 1.0.37.42 compiled in (Health Connect and its 18 permissions, the LAN sync natives, the https App Link, `expo-print`, `expo-notifications`, Firebase's `google-services.json`, `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`, and `plugins/withCleartextLan.js` without which the plain-HTTP LAN fetch fails on Android 9+) and the dated list of when each of those features was wired up in JS are in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`. `https://insidestoryapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` is hosted on Cloudflare (Worker `inside-story-site`, deployed from `docs/app-links`, see its README), so the App Link verifies on install, and the same Worker serves landing pages at `/connect` and `/import-shared` for a phone without the app.

Five items written up on 2026-08-30 after a review of Meal Engine. Every one of them is still open and still parked in the Project Tracker: they were moved here because the brief had reached its size ceiling and these are long-form reasoning rather than standing rules. The pointer left in CLAUDE.md names all five.

22. **"Get Back on Track": recovering a day after a missed or off-plan meal.** Same 2026-08-30 review. Meal Engine's positioning line is "One bad meal shouldn't ruin your whole week," and its plan rebalances automatically on a deviation. This app already records a deliberate exception honestly (`outside_eating_window`, 2026-08-29/30) but nothing actively recovers the day once it goes sideways. Most pieces already exist: `getDailyNutrientAnalysis` knows what has actually been eaten so far, `generateDailyMealPlan` can regenerate a single day, and `resolveMealPlanTimes` already fits meals to a declared eating window. The work is wiring them into one action that regenerates the remainder of today around what actually happened. Framing stays exactly as it is now: a missed or off-plan meal is a recorded exception to look at, never a failure to score.
23. **A weekly check-in that retunes targets from nutrient, weight and symptom trends together.** Same 2026-08-30 review. Meal Engine retunes calorie and macro targets weekly from the weight trend alone; this app's `user_nutrient_targets` are manual overrides in Profile. Copy the cadence, not the input: retune from nutrient gaps, weight trend, AND symptom/flare trends at once, the last of which Meal Engine structurally cannot use since it holds no symptom data, making this a differentiator rather than catch-up. Must follow the standing rule already applied to healing stages: the app suggests a change and the person accepts it, never a silent reclassification.
24. **TRACK mode: targets and a running total, no generated meal plan.** Same 2026-08-30 review. Meal Engine's PLAN versus TRACK split concedes that not everyone wants to be told what to cook; this app's meal planning is PLAN-only. A mode toggle in the Daily Meal Plan lens showing targets and a running total against them, with no generated meals, reusing `applyNutrientTargetOverrides` and the existing daily nutrient analysis. Small build, and it serves anyone who wants the condition intelligence without a generated menu.
25. **Menstrual cycle tracking, cross-referenced in Pattern Finder.** Same 2026-08-30 review, which ships cycle integration. This app has no cycle concept at all despite tracking PCOS, Hashimoto's, Graves', Migraine and Rheumatoid Arthritis, all with documented cycle interactions. Worth building for the condition angle rather than to match a competitor: a small cycle table cross-referenced in Pattern Finder, so a pattern such as flares clustering in one phase surfaces on its own, an insight Meal Engine cannot reach. Needs its own cited research pass per relevant condition before any claim is shown on screen, same discipline as every other Digest claim.
26. **Adopt "allergen-aware, not allergy-safe" wording.** Same 2026-08-30 review, borrowing their disclaimer phrase verbatim because it describes what this app actually does. Allergy matching here is best-effort substring matching (`app/(tabs)/log.tsx`'s food-trial picker, reused by `lib/foodPersonalization.ts`), and those five words state that honestly, fitting the standing evidence-honesty discipline better than any wording currently shipped. Needs a sweep for every place allergen filtering is surfaced, not one screen, per the standing global-rules rule.


## Phases 1 and 2 of the cross-app push, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23

The two full build accounts, condensed in the brief to a pointer plus the two rules they established.

**Where did I put it (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.6), phase 1 of the six-phase cross-app push.** Three sources, one search, and one rule holding the whole thing up: a location nobody has confirmed in months sends somebody to an empty cupboard, which leaves them worse off than saying nothing. So a place carries its age everywhere it is shown, and `placeConfidence` plus `stalePrompt` (`lib/whereIsIt.ts`, pure, 48 checks in `scripts/test_where_is_it.js`) warn without ever claiming the thing moved. `kitchen_items` gained `location` and `location_set_at`, kept apart from `added_at` on purpose: confirming where something is makes the ANSWER current again without claiming the food is fresh. The other two sources are read only, capture notes sorted to the new `place` destination (the sentence stays whole, since guessing which half is the place is how the app starts being wrong about somebody's house) and plantings still growing, whose place is their area. `lib/whereIsItDb.ts` reads all three, `app/where-is-it.tsx` is the screen, and the places offered as chips are read back out of the rows using them rather than kept in a table, which is what makes it an open list with nothing to orphan. It is a top-level Home row directly under Capture rather than a lens, because the moment it serves is somebody standing in front of an open cupboard. Works in full on Windows; only the voice half of capture is phone-only.

**Trends > What You Eat (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.7), phase 2 of the same push.** A lens is a SUBJECT holding several bands behind the fold, the way Nutrients already holds every nutrient, which is how roughly twenty proposed charts take Trends from 10 lenses to 14 rather than to 30. This one is how wide the eating is: how many different foods a week plus three near things off the safe list, what keeps coming back and the gap between repeats, fermented and gut-supporting foods a week, the cooking method mix, bought ready against made at home, and how the safe list has grown. **A week with nothing logged draws as a gap, never as a zero**, which is the rule the lens rests on and which holds for every periodic chart built after it: being too busy to log is not a week of eating nothing, so every weekly figure in `lib/eatingVariety.ts` (pure, 203 checks in `scripts/test_eating_variety.js`) is `number | null`, a blank row reads "not logged", and the count of blank weeks sits under the headline. It also rules out a line chart for a series with gaps, since a line either joins across the blank (inventing a week) or plots it at zero. Two readings were taken from what the tables hold rather than from what would have been convenient: bought against home-made reads the reference database's `foods.category` (`CommercialPremade` and `MyProcessedFoods`, which is what a barcode scan becomes), since `meals.source_type` is hard-coded `'manual'` for every row, and gut-supporting reads the already-scored, already-cited Microbiome Effects tier (`sub_criterion_id` 20) rather than a keyword list invented here, with fermentation counted on top through `cooking_method` plus a short name list that deliberately excludes pickled. An unresolved free-text meal item still counts toward how many different foods got eaten, carrying no claim about where it came from. `lib/eatingVarietyDb.ts` does the three reads in one bulk query per range. Fiber got a headline band at the top of the **Nutrients** lens instead, and deliberately did NOT join `CORE_NUTRIENT_CODES`, which also drives Home's fuel rings and the Overview report. Home gained `varietyThisWeek` beside This Week's Trend: weekTrend counts what got flagged, this counts how wide the eating was.

27. **External data program: nine public-data lookup projects behind one Cloudflare Worker.** Brainstormed and written up 2026-09-14 into the [Project Tracker](https://app.notion.com/p/c9597dcb8a1d4cc5bc34ef87a4a097df) as nine Deferred "Coming project" rows plus one Decision row, [External lookups: three privacy shapes, one Worker](https://app.notion.com/p/3db53652f272816d8051f1d335574853). Nothing is built. This is accepted scope rather than a loose idea, so read those rows before re-deriving any of it. The rule settled first, which every outside request follows: (1) a keyed lookup, a barcode or product name in and a label out, routed through the `inside-story-site` Worker off a D1 snapshot with the edge cache in front, so only the key leaves the phone; (2) anything keyed by condition, which the Worker pre-fetches for all 19 on a schedule and the phone downloads as a whole bundle, so a device never makes a per-condition request; (3) anything keyed by location, coarsened to a rounded coordinate or a city and never the precise fix, stated in-product the way the voice boundary is stated, and opt-in. The nine projects, each with its sources named in those rows: supplement labels by barcode, packaged foods (which also moves `lib/barcodeLookup.ts`'s direct calls and its bundled USDA API key behind the Worker), OTC medicines by barcode and prescriptions by name, recall matching against what a person scanned or saved, weather, barometric pressure, UV and air quality in Pattern Finder, current clinical trials per condition, the stated reference-database gaps as unified-pipeline adapters, garden, soil and Earth Matters data, and PubMed citation verification for every Digest reference. Agreed order: recalls and weather first, then supplement and OTC barcode work together. Cost baseline is Workers Paid at $5/month from the day the first lookup ships, with monthly snapshot refreshes run by a GitHub Actions cron loading into fresh tables and swapping by rename. One product rule carried over: when a refresh brings a newer record for something already saved, the app offers it on next open and never silently replaces what the person confirmed.

28. **The daily-living program for the second audience, eleven Project Tracker rows written 2026-09-16.** Follows from the "Who it is for" section above: somebody whose reason for opening this app is that daily life will not stay in their head. Nine Open Feature rows, one Deferred Feature row and one Deferred Decision row, so read those rather than re-deriving any of it. In rough order of value for the effort: a **capture inbox** (one control, voice or text, no category chosen at capture time, sorted afterwards); **reminders for everything else carrying a date** (bills, upkeep, expiring benefits, garden tasks, plus a nudge-until-done mode with its own switch); **reminders that land before a thing rather than at it** (a lead time per kind, overridable per item); **step-by-step routines** shown one step at a time; **"did I already do it" and "where did I put it"**; **Simple View plus one clear next thing on Home**; **a way in that does not require a condition**, the row that decides whether any of the rest is ever seen, and which needs the Free tier line re-drawn deliberately; a **logged-variety alert** in Insights > Nutrients, framed as what is thin plus three near things, never as eating badly; **sensory attributes on foods plus food chaining in Safe Foods**, deferred because no source carries the data and the choice between hand-curation and derivation has to be made first; and **whether ADHD and autism become selectable profiles**, deferred on the question of how to give them framing and check-in tags without the condition scoring implying that diet treats them. ## Two desktop paragraphs in full, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23

Condensed to pointers in the pass that added phase 5 of the cross-app push. Both rules they carry stay in CLAUDE.md; what is here is the detail behind them.

- **On a computer OneDrive is the folder on the disk, and there is no sign-in** (1.0.42.25). The phone signs in to Microsoft Graph because Android will not let an app pick a OneDrive folder; that sign-in ends at a `hashimotosapp://` redirect nothing on a PC is registered for, so it waited for a result that could never come. `lib/oneDriveAuth.ts` reports signed in on desktop and `lib/oneDriveGraph.ts` sends every one of its calls to `lib/desktop/cloudFolder.ts`, which addresses a folder as `driveId 'disk'` with the absolute path as its `itemId` in the same `app_meta` row, so nothing in `lib/db.ts`, `lib/syncInbox.ts` or the backup code changed. `desktop/cloudFolder.js` does the file work in the main process: roots from `OneDriveConsumer`, `OneDrive` and `OneDriveCommercial`, a write landing as a temp file then a rename so the OneDrive client never uploads a half-written backup, and writes refused outside a detected root, the home folder, or a folder picked through the OS dialog this run. A folder travels between the two kinds of device by its sentence, "OneDrive / Apps / Inside Story", mapped back onto the disk by `folderFromPhonePath` and onto Graph by `folderFromComputerPath`.

- **Layout on a wide window.** `lib/menuFit.ts` owns it: TabHub's card centered on the window (`menuCardLeft`; a phone keeps its left anchor), hub menus spanning the whole phone width or the desktop window's 480 dp starting width (`hubMenuCardSpan`, TabHub in two rows of six and five, a lens menu three rows tall and scrolling), corner hubs a fixed distance from TabHub rather than from the corner (`cornerHubLeft`, `secondaryHubCardLeft`), and `PageIdentityLabel` at its starting width (`pageIdentityBoxSpan`). Text size is Chromium page zoom kept by `desktop/zoom.js` (125% by default, Ctrl and + / - / 0, a View menu, a Text size picker in Profile). **The corner box and `VersionLabel` zoom with the artwork and are deliberately NOT pinned against desktop text size**: a 1.0.42.23 pin held them at fixed pixels while the artwork zoomed and was undone by direct instruction in 1.0.42.24 ("match how the mobile version is done"). Do not re-add it. On web `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` calls `enableScreens(true)` at module level, without which every visited tab stays drawn under the current one, and a tap on another hub's button while a menu is open lands on that hub through the focus-gated registry in `lib/hubHandoff.ts`.


## The peer-sync paragraph in full, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23

Condensed in the pass that added phase 5 of the cross-app push. What was taken out: `PERSONAL_HEALTH_TABLES` (21 tables) exists to be asserted against rather than consulted; `lib/peerSyncDevice.ts` keeps the agreed copy per person in `peer_sync_base`, deliberately not device local, since both of this person's devices talk to the same partner; the payload is version 2 (`lib/partnerSync.ts`); the `ready: false` flag flips the day there is somewhere to keep another person's records apart from this person's; covered by `scripts/test_peer_relationships.js` (123 checks) and `test_peer_merge.js` (56).

- **1.0.49.4: that same process runs between two people, not only between one person's devices.** Direct instruction: "the communication flow as per what is being done between the user's devices needs to be the same kind of process that happens between partners, and their children, and where applicable, their care giver." The engine is the same engine (`mergeTables`), and everything added on top of it is the boundary. Full account in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`. What stands: **`lib/peerRelationships.ts` is the inverse of the device rule, an ALLOWLIST**, since two devices hold one database between them while two people hold two and almost nothing belongs to both, so nothing crosses unless a relationship names it and `tablesThatCross()` is that list. Three ways a person can hold something: `shared` (both change it, so it merges), `theirs` (one owns it and the other keeps a copy, so a copy replaces), `onTheirBehalf` (both write and it merges, and the records belong to the other person). An area marked `ready: false` (`schedule`, `meds`, `symptoms`) carries no table at all, so no caller can send it by accident, and the flag flips the day there is somewhere to keep another person's records apart from this person's. `PERSONAL_HEALTH_TABLES` (21 tables) is there to be asserted against rather than consulted. `lib/peerMerge.ts` refuses and names a whole table outside the list rather than dropping it in silence, and keeps single columns on this phone (`keepsHome`), without which a partner ticking a line off would blank the note underneath it. `lib/peerSyncDevice.ts` keeps the agreed copy per person in `peer_sync_base`, deliberately not device local, since both of this person's devices talk to the same partner. The payload is version 2 (`lib/partnerSync.ts`), filtered through `tablesToSend` on the way OUT, since a privacy decision is either enforced in one place or hoped for in several. **`talksAutomatically(role)` replaced every `role === 'partner'` transport gate** in all five carriers, so they reach a child or caregiver link the moment its setting-up ships. Covered by `scripts/test_peer_relationships.js` (123 checks) and `test_peer_merge.js` (56).

## Phases 1 to 5 of the cross-app push in full, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23

Condensed into one account of the finished six-phase push when phase 6 shipped (1.0.50.11).
The standing rules from these paragraphs (a lens is a subject, a gap is never a zero, the
local-day rule, units are never converted across kinds, only money recorded against a day)
all survive in CLAUDE.md; what follows is the build narrative behind them, verbatim.

**Phases 1 and 2 of the six-phase cross-app push (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.6 and 1.0.50.7), condensed.** Full accounts in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "Phases 1 and 2 of the cross-app push, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23". **Where did I put it** is one search over three sources (`kitchen_items.location`, capture notes sorted to `place`, plantings still growing), reached as a top-level Home row, a place carrying its age everywhere it is shown so a stale answer warns rather than claiming the thing moved (`lib/whereIsIt.ts`, `lib/whereIsItDb.ts`, `app/where-is-it.tsx`). **Trends > What You Eat** is how wide the eating is, week by week (`lib/eatingVariety.ts`, `lib/eatingVarietyDb.ts`, Home's `varietyThisWeek`). Two rules from those two phases hold for everything built after them:

1. **A lens is a SUBJECT holding several bands behind the fold**, the way Nutrients holds every nutrient. That is what takes roughly twenty proposed charts from 30 lenses down to 14. The record lives on its tab and the timeline lives on Trends.
2. **A period with nothing logged draws as a gap, never as a zero.** Being too busy to log is not a week of eating nothing, so every periodic figure is `number | null`, a blank row says so in words, and the count of blank periods sits under the headline. It also rules out a line chart for a gapped series, since a line either joins across the blank (inventing a period) or plots it at zero.

**Trends > Keeping Up (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.8), phase 3 of the same push.** The lens for the second audience: somebody who has capture, reminders and routines, and nothing telling them how any of it is going. Five bands, each reading a record that already existed somewhere on Life: what gets ticked off (`done_checks`), routines walked and the step they stop on, what gets captured and how long it waits to be sorted, upkeep done on time against late, and how work has felt. **Nothing on it scores anybody**, which is the rule it rests on and which `scripts/test_keeping_up.js` enforces with a sweep for the words a scoring app would use. Two things follow. A day with no mark is not a day undone: the app knows when somebody tapped something, not what they did, so a blank day says no mark was made and a blank week reads "nothing marked" rather than zero, carried by `renderWeekRows`'s per-caller `emptyLabel` because "not logged" is right for meals and wrong here. And a thin week is said plainly with nothing attached to it.

**Two tables were added for that phase, not one**, both append-only on the `done_check_marks` precedent: `routine_runs`, which is opened when a walk STARTS rather than when it finishes, so an abandoned walk is still on the record, and `upkeep_doings`, since `markUpkeepDone` overwrites a single `last_done_on` and band 4 would have been a snapshot for good. Both start on 2026-09-23 with nothing behind them, so those two bands say they count from the day they started keeping every one. The reasoning, and the two guards that keep a run from being opened or inflated twice, are in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "Phase 3's two new tables, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23".

**The local-day rule, which every later reader of these tables needs.** `done_check_marks.marked_at`, `capture_notes.created_at` and `routine_runs.started_at` all store `new Date().toISOString()`, which is UTC. Slicing ten characters off one gives the UTC day, so six hours west of Greenwich every evening mark lands on tomorrow and a run of evening marks reads as no run at all. `dayOf` in `lib/keepingUpDb.ts` goes through a `Date` and returns the LOCAL day, the way `describeMarkMoment` in `lib/routines.ts` always has, and each SQL window reaches a day past the range at both ends before being narrowed in JS. `upkeep_doings.done_on` and `work_checkins.week_of` are plain dates and need none of it. `lib/keepingUp.ts` is pure and holds every sentence (424 checks), `lib/keepingUpDb.ts` does the reads, and Home gained a `keepingUp` card in the Trends group: the longest run leads, with whatever is waiting under it. Still open from this phase's scope: the regulation and sensory tags becoming a band inside the existing Symptoms & Flares lens.

**Trends > Garden Yield (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.9), phase 4 of the same push.** Four bands over the whole life of a garden, and the first lens in the push that needed no new table: `garden_harvests`, `garden_plantings`, `compost_events`, `harvest_dispositions` and `harvest_shares_received` all keep their full history already, and all five store plain local dates, so none of phase 3's `dayOf` machinery applies. What it reads: weight month by month with a share per crop and per area, days to harvest expected against actual, compost taken out of a pile against compost put on an area, and what has gone out to other people or come back from them. **A garden earns over seasons, so this one counts in months and gets its own range pills** (12 months, 2 years, everything, the last resolved from `getEarliestGardenDate()`), rather than the 7, 30 and 90 days every other lens shares. The gap rule above still holds and is worded for the subject: a blank month is left blank and counted, and the note under it says a quiet month is often simply out of season, since nothing in the data separates that from a month nobody logged.

**Units are never converted across kinds, which is what the whole lens rests on.** Grams, kilos, ounces and pounds add through `convertToGrams`; a count of cucumbers is a count and never becomes a weight; anything else (bunches, buckets) stays on a line of its own. So a percentage is only ever taken of a weight, and a crop somebody counts rather than weighs carries no share beside it. The same refusal runs through band 3, where `COMPOST_AMOUNT_UNITS` mixes buckets with kilos, so compost totals stay per unit. A month with pickings but no weight in it gets a zero and a sentence saying what was picked, deliberately not a gap, since `null` is reserved for a month with no harvest row at all. `lib/harvestYield.ts` is pure and holds every figure and sentence (612 checks in `scripts/test_harvest_yield.js`), `lib/harvestYieldDb.ts` does six ranged reads, and Garden > Harvest Log gained a row through to the lens rather than a chart, so **Garden stays at eight lenses**. Home gained `gardenYield` in the Trends group (a card's group is the tab it opens): this calendar month's weight, and what that would have cost at prices the person has recorded paying, which is money not spent rather than money made, said in those words, with the crops having no recorded price counted and left out.

**Trends > What It Costs (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.10), phase 5 of the same push.** The most wiring of any lens in the push: four bands over seven tables on three tabs (`finance_entries`, `finance_medical_bills`, `therapy_sessions`, `grocery_list_items`, `garden_cost_details`, `treatments`, `treatment_nutrients`). What a condition has cost month by month with insurance separated from care and each bill's condition named, what eating this way comes to a day with groceries beside dining out and what came back out of the kitchen, what a garden cost for the weight it gave against shop prices the person has recorded paying, and what supplements cost beside what food by itself is reaching. It counts in months and shares Garden Yield's range pills, resolving Everything from `getEarliestMoneyDate()` rather than `getEarliestGardenDate()`, so a garden logged since 2019 with one receipt entered last month draws no blank years. `lib/costOfEating.ts` is pure and holds every figure and sentence (1,139 checks in `scripts/test_cost_of_eating.js`), `lib/costOfEatingDb.ts` does nine reads in one pass, and `getHarvestsForRange` was added to `lib/harvestYieldDb.ts` so this lens and Garden Yield can never disagree about what was picked. **No Home card, deliberately**: what a condition costs is not a thing to be met with on opening the app.

**Three boundaries that lens rests on, each of which a later session will be tempted to soften.** (1) **Life > Finances stays the ledger.** Every account, bill, budget and total lives there and nothing on Trends writes, so this lens takes only the four questions a ledger cannot answer, which is also why band 1 is not a second copy of `components/FinanceHealthSection.tsx`, whose all-time-since rollup cannot show a shape month by month. (2) **Only money recorded against a day is counted.** `finance_recurring` rules are left out on purpose, since drawing a history out of a rule about what should happen every month would invent spending in months nobody entered any. There is no link column between `finance_medical_bills` and `finance_entries` either, so anything entered in both places is counted from both and the note under band 1 states both facts rather than pretending to de-duplicate. (3) **Band 4 never says a supplement was unnecessary.** It reports that a target is now being met by food, which is the stated goal, and carries that sentence in the band itself. Two smaller decisions hold with it: condition names come from `listAllConditions()` rather than `getTrackedConditionsWithNames()`, so a bill tagged to a condition somebody has since stopped tracking still shows its name instead of a bare code, and the food side of band 4 reads one 30-day window for only the nutrients of supplements that ENDED inside the range, which is what keeps it from being ruinously slow.

**From your garden (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.11), phase 6 and the last of the push.** The only piece that needed new capture, which is why it went last: it says nothing at all until it has been used for a season. Saving a meal offers to take what that meal used off what the garden still has on hand, and the draw-down happens in the same tap. `lib/plateSource.ts` is pure and holds the matching and every sentence (1,087 checks in `scripts/test_plate_source.js`), `lib/plateSourceDb.ts` does the reads and the one write, `lib/gardenPlateOffer.ts` carries a single listener, and `components/GardenPlateOfferHost.tsx` is the sheet, mounted once at the app root on the `components/TellClaudeHost.tsx` shape because a meal is saved from several screens and the sheet has to paint over the window from any of them, including from inside a builder's modal. Every call site is the one line `offerGardenUse(mealId)`: `app/voice-log.tsx` (3), `components/FindMealView.tsx` (3) and `components/MealBuilder.tsx` (1). `components/ScanProductView.tsx` was surveyed and deliberately left out, since a scanned product's food id ends in `|Scanned` and can never match a picking. **No new lens and no Home card**: the two bands land on lenses already built, the garden share of what gets eaten on What You Eat and what that share came to on What It Costs, so **Trends stays at 14**.

**Four decisions that phase rests on.** (1) **`harvest_uses` is a new append-only table**, on the `upkeep_doings` precedent, with no foreign key at all and `food_name` carried on the row, because `meal_items` has no provenance column and `replaceMealItems` deletes and re-inserts on every edit, so anything keyed to a meal item would be orphaned by the next edit. `recordHarvestUsage` stays the one thing that changes `quantity_remaining`; `harvest_uses` is the history beside it, written in the same call so the two cannot drift. (2) **Every row in the sheet starts ticked and can be unticked**, because a tomato from the fridge and a tomato from the shop look the same to the app, so the person settles it and nothing comes off a picking that fed nobody. (3) **An amount comes off only where the meal recorded the picking's unit**, rule 4 above: where it did not, `quantity_used` is written as 0, the row is still the record that the garden fed somebody, `quantity_remaining` is untouched, and the offer line says so and points at Garden > Harvest Log. That amountless row still counts a food on the share band, which counts foods on a plate rather than weight, and is left out of the money figure with a sentence saying why. (4) **A logged food counts as home grown only where a picking was marked on the same local day under the same name**, which undercounts rather than guessing, and the caveat under the band says so. The money band values only the part that reached a plate where Garden Yield values everything picked, so its boundary sentence says the two read the same pickings different ways rather than adding together.

The same pass also shortened three items of the six-item push list above this section. Those three verbatim:

3. **Trends > Keeping Up** (1.0.50.8), the lens for the second audience: somebody who has capture, reminders and routines and nothing telling them how any of it is going. Five bands, each reading a record that already existed on Life. `lib/keepingUp.ts` (424 checks) and `lib/keepingUpDb.ts`, Home's `keepingUp`. Two new append-only tables: `routine_runs`, opened when a walk STARTS rather than when it finishes so an abandoned walk is still on the record, and `upkeep_doings`, since `markUpkeepDone` overwrites a single `last_done_on` and band 4 would have been a snapshot for good. Both started empty on 2026-09-23, which those two bands say. **Nothing on it scores anybody**, enforced by a forbidden-words sweep in `scripts/test_keeping_up.js`. Still open from its scope: the regulation and sensory tags becoming a band inside the existing Symptoms & Flares lens.

5. **Trends > What It Costs** (1.0.50.10), the most wiring of any lens in the push: four bands over seven tables on three tabs (`finance_entries`, `finance_medical_bills`, `therapy_sessions`, `grocery_list_items`, `garden_cost_details`, `treatments`, `treatment_nutrients`). Months again, resolving Everything from `getEarliestMoneyDate()` so a garden logged since 2019 with one receipt entered last month draws no blank years. `lib/costOfEating.ts` (1,139 checks) and `lib/costOfEatingDb.ts`. **No Home card, deliberately**: what a condition costs is not a thing to be met with on opening the app.

6. **From your garden** (1.0.50.11), which has its own two paragraphs below.

And two Garden paragraphs, shortened in the same pass. Verbatim as they stood:

**Garden, the indoor grow (2026-09-21, 1.0.42.10).** Indoors, the light is the sun: an indoor area's form asks about its lights (kind, make, count, watts, hours a day, timer, spectrum, the plant stage it suits) in place of the sun question, a greenhouse asks the sun question plus Lights added?, and outdoors asks the sun question only; `sunlight_exposure` is stored null for an indoor area. Every area has a **Grow Setup** (`garden_equipment`, `lib/growSetupDb.ts`, `components/GrowSetupSection.tsx`): lights, containers, hydroponics, fans, filters, climate control, timers, meters and any kind the person names, each with a purchase recorded as a growing cost under the area and an ongoing amount on a cadence, and a piece with a purchase or history marked no longer in use rather than deleted. **Electricity** is a band under Growing Costs (`components/ElectricityBand.tsx`): the bill from before the grow is the baseline, every bill after it is compared per day so a 28-day bill and a 33-day bill compare fairly, and the monthly difference is recorded as a growing cost (kind `electricity`) only when the person asks, never on its own. Ongoing amounts stay in the garden and are not pushed into `finance_recurring`. The arithmetic and every sentence live in `lib/growSetup.ts`, covered by `scripts/test_grow_setup.js`.

**Days Until, a counter for anything (2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22, 1.0.42.12 through 1.0.42.15 and 1.0.49.7).** Two tables on one arithmetic (`lib/countdown.ts`, `scripts/test_countdown.js`): `garden_countdowns`, tied to an area and optionally to one planting, and `countdowns`, tied to nothing, which is a second table rather than a nullable `plot_id` because a garden counter travels to Past Areas with its area and counts toward whether that area still has records, and a free one does neither. A counter counts whole calendar days, reads Today on its day and keeps counting as "N days over" past it rather than hiding; Done keeps it as the record of how long the thing took. `components/DaysUntilSection.tsx` takes a `scope` of `garden`, `free` or `everything`, which is how one component serves Garden > Days Until, Life > Days Until and two Home cards. Both kinds raise the same `countdown` dated reminder, firing once on the landing day and deliberately outside `NUDGES_WHILE_OVERDUE`, since a counter past its day keeps counting on screen by design. ## The archiving pass of 2026-09-23, part 1: the push block, navigation and the supplement paragraphs

CLAUDE.md had reached 99.6 KB against the ~100 KB ceiling its own "How this document works" section sets, so a systematic pass moved build accounts here and left the standing rules in the brief. Each passage below is verbatim as it stood before the pass.

### The food-first paragraph, shortened

**Food first, and a supplement only for what food cannot supply.** Direct statement, 2026-09-22: "the goal is to modify how a person eats so with their food they are receiving an optimal amount of every one of them and not have to take any supplements, but to also make sure that you do take the ones you cannot receive from your food because of whatever reason, such as being vegan, or alergic, etc." A target reached by food and the same target reached by a capsule are two different outcomes, and everywhere the app shows a nutrient amount it has to say which one happened. Two halves, and neither is advice to stop taking anything: show which supplements a person's eating has already made unnecessary, and show which ones their diet cannot cover, so those keep being taken. Built in four places, each accounted for in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "The food-versus-supplement build account, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23": Insights > Nutrients, Home's Today's Fuel Gauges, My Meds at the moment a supplement is added, and Trends > Nutrients over the whole charted range. **The supplement half is always worked out per day from each supplement's start and end dates** (`getSupplementNutrientTotalsByDate`, `lib/supplementWindow.ts`), never from today's regimen stretched backwards, which read a supplement started yesterday as having been there in June. Nothing in this app records a dose being swallowed, so where a person gave no dates the supplement is counted across the range and the caption says so.

### The supplement-timing paragraph, shortened

**When a supplement is taken belongs to scheduling, and it matters.** Same statement: supplements carry rules about with or without food, with water or with fat, not with certain foods, and not with other vitamins, minerals, acids and hormones they compete with, synergistic and antagonistic both. Those rules live in the interaction-rules engine and the dose timeline in Schedules > Meds. Schedules > Today's Meals is the day itself, meals and doses interleaved by the clock, and an opened dose reads the meals around it (1.0.49.6; `lib/doseMealTiming.ts` checks a dose against the nearest qualifying MEAL, which `lib/interactionRules.ts` never did, and `getDayMealAndDoseTimeline` in `lib/db.ts` assembles the day). Two things there stay true whatever gets built on top of them: `MEAL_AMOUNT_THAT_MATTERS` is a set of working thresholds rather than doses from a trial, which is why every sentence it generates names the amount itself rather than asking to be trusted, and a meal with nothing resolvable to the food database reads as could not be checked, never as carrying nothing. Nothing on that lens writes; times, taken, skipped and removed stay on Meds, so one place holds that record. The build account is in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`.

### The six-phase push block and the stage 0 write-up, as they stood before the pass

**The six-phase cross-app push is finished (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.6 through 1.0.50.11).** Six things that each read a record already being kept and had nowhere to be read. Per-phase accounts are in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "Phases 1 and 2 of the cross-app push, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23", "Phase 3's two new tables, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23" and "Phases 1 to 5 of the cross-app push in full, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23". What was built:

1. **Where did I put it** (1.0.50.6), one search over three sources (`kitchen_items.location`, capture notes sorted to `place`, plantings still growing), reached as a top-level Home row, a place carrying its age everywhere it is shown so a stale answer warns rather than claiming the thing moved. `lib/whereIsIt.ts`, `lib/whereIsItDb.ts`, `app/where-is-it.tsx`.
2. **Trends > What You Eat** (1.0.50.7), how wide the eating is, week by week. `lib/eatingVariety.ts`, `lib/eatingVarietyDb.ts`, Home's `varietyThisWeek`.
3. **Trends > Keeping Up** (1.0.50.8), the lens for the second audience: somebody who has capture, reminders and routines and nothing telling them how any of it is going. Five bands, each reading a record that already existed on Life. `lib/keepingUp.ts` (424 checks) and `lib/keepingUpDb.ts`, Home's `keepingUp`. Two new append-only tables, `routine_runs` (opened when a walk STARTS, so an abandoned walk is still on the record) and `upkeep_doings` (since `markUpkeepDone` overwrites a single `last_done_on`), both started empty on 2026-09-23, which those two bands say. **Nothing on it scores anybody**, enforced by a forbidden-words sweep in `scripts/test_keeping_up.js`. Still open from its scope: the regulation and sensory tags becoming a band inside the existing Symptoms & Flares lens.
4. **Trends > Garden Yield** (1.0.50.9), four bands over the whole life of a garden and the first lens in the push needing no new table. A garden earns over seasons, so it counts in MONTHS with range pills of its own (12 months, 2 years, everything from `getEarliestGardenDate()`) rather than the 7, 30 and 90 days every other lens shares. `lib/harvestYield.ts` (612 checks) and `lib/harvestYieldDb.ts`. Reached by a row on Garden > Harvest Log rather than a chart, so **Garden stays at eight lenses**; Home's `gardenYield`.
5. **Trends > What It Costs** (1.0.50.10), the most wiring of any lens in the push: four bands over seven tables on three tabs. Months again, resolving Everything from `getEarliestMoneyDate()`. `lib/costOfEating.ts` (1,139 checks) and `lib/costOfEatingDb.ts`. **No Home card, deliberately**: what a condition costs is not a thing to be met with on opening the app.
6. **From your garden** (1.0.50.11), described in the paragraph below.

**Five rules the push settled, each of which a later session will be tempted to soften.**

1. **A lens is a SUBJECT holding several bands behind the fold**, the way Nutrients holds every nutrient, which is what took roughly twenty proposed charts down to 14 lenses. The record lives on its tab and the timeline lives on Trends, so nothing on Trends writes.
2. **A period with nothing logged draws as a gap, never as a zero.** Being too busy to log is not a week of eating nothing, so every periodic figure is `number | null`, a blank period says so in words (`renderWeekRows` takes an `emptyLabel` per caller, since "not logged" is right for meals and "nothing marked" is right for a day somebody tapped nothing), and the count of blank periods sits under the headline. It also rules out a line chart for a gapped series, since a line either joins across the blank, inventing a period, or plots it at zero.
3. **The local-day rule, which every later reader of these tables needs.** `done_check_marks.marked_at`, `capture_notes.created_at` and `routine_runs.started_at` store `new Date().toISOString()`, which is UTC, so slicing ten characters off one puts every evening mark west of Greenwich on tomorrow and reads a run of evening marks as no run at all. `dayOf` in `lib/keepingUpDb.ts` goes through a `Date` for the LOCAL day, the way `describeMarkMoment` in `lib/routines.ts` always has, and each SQL window reaches a day past the range at both ends before being narrowed in JS. Plain date columns (`upkeep_doings.done_on`, `work_checkins.week_of`, `harvest_uses.used_on`, every garden table) need none of it.
4. **Units are never converted across kinds.** Grams, kilos, ounces and pounds add through `convertToGrams`; a count of cucumbers is a count and never becomes a weight; anything else (bunches, buckets) stays on a line of its own, which is also why `COMPOST_AMOUNT_UNITS` totals stay per unit. So a percentage or a price is only ever taken of a weight, and a crop somebody counts rather than weighs carries no share beside it.
5. **Only money recorded against a day is counted, and a figure is never guessed at.** `finance_recurring` rules are left out, since drawing a history out of a rule about what should happen every month would invent spending in months nobody entered any. There is no link column between `finance_medical_bills` and `finance_entries`, so anything entered in both places is counted from both and the note under the band states that rather than pretending to de-duplicate. Money on a harvest is worked out only from prices the person has recorded paying for the same food in the same unit, is an avoided cost rather than income, and says both. And band 4 of What It Costs never says a supplement was unnecessary, only that a target is now being met by food, which is the stated goal.

**From your garden (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.11), phase 6 and the last of the push.** The only piece that needed new capture, which is why it went last: saving a meal offers to take what that meal used off what the garden still has on hand, and the draw-down happens in the same tap. Its two bands land on lenses already built, the garden share of what gets eaten on What You Eat and what that share came to on What It Costs, so **Trends stays at 14** and there is no Home card. `lib/plateSource.ts` is pure (1,087 checks), `lib/plateSourceDb.ts` does the reads and the one write, `components/GardenPlateOfferHost.tsx` is the sheet mounted at the app root because a meal is saved from several screens, and every call site is the one line `offerGardenUse(mealId)`. `harvest_uses` is append-only with no foreign key and `food_name` on the row, since `meal_items` has no provenance column and `replaceMealItems` deletes and re-inserts on every edit. Every row in the sheet starts ticked and can be unticked, because a tomato from the fridge and a tomato from the shop look the same to the app. **The fuller account, including the four decisions it rests on, is in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "Phase 6 of the cross-app push in full, removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23".**

**Growing conditions as a record, and the sensor plan behind it (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.12).** Eleven `garden_*` tables held what was planted, spent, picked and eaten, and not one held a measurement of the conditions any of it grew in. The idea a later session will be tempted to skip past: **separate the reading from the radio.** A soil moisture figure is worth the same whether it arrived over WiFi or came off a $12 meter, so the record gets built first and every way of filling it is a later, optional addition. Four stages were proposed and **only stage 0 is approved and built**: stage 1 is DIY LAN sensors over the zeroconf and static-server code already compiled in, stage 2 cameras over RTSP or ONVIF (a native module and a rebuild), stage 3 commercial cloud accounts over OAuth. Three corrections to the outside advice that started this bind whatever gets built later: **no time-series database**, since SQLite handles a sensor's rate and a second engine breaks local-first; **no Flutter and no Node or Python backend**, since Expo is settled and a backend is the one thing this app deliberately lacks; and **nothing is built on Home Assistant**, since requiring a hub disqualifies the audience. The phone is the hub.

What stage 0 is: `garden_readings`, one append-only table on the `harvest_uses` precedent, with no foreign key, `plot_name` carried on the row so a Past Area keeps its readings readable, and a `source` of `hand` or `device` that exists now so stage 1 needs no migration and a blank month can tell nothing came in from nothing was measured. A reading is deletable, since a mistyped figure has to be fixable. `measurement_kind` is the fifth open list and the first that is not movable: readings are history, so a measurement name with readings against it retires and stays readable rather than asking for a reassignment. **Units are turned into one another only where the two mean the same quantity** (°C and °F, mm and in, L and gal, mS/cm and µS/cm); a moisture percentage and a tensiometer centibar are deliberately not a family, nor are lux and PPFD, so readings in the odd unit out are set aside with a line saying how many and in what. Rain and water given are added up over a month, everything else averaged with its lowest and highest, since an average soil temperature hides the night that dropped below freezing. Garden > Growing Conditions is the ninth Garden lens and where a reading goes in; Trends > Growing Conditions is the fifteenth Trends lens, three bands over months the way Garden Yield counts, and reads only. `lib/growingConditions.ts` is pure (1,292 checks in `scripts/test_growing_conditions.js`, whose forbidden-words sweep adds "too low", "too high", "ideal", "optimal" and "healthy range", since a conditions figure is the easiest place in this app to start telling somebody their soil is wrong) and `lib/growingConditionsDb.ts` does the reads and the two writes. No Home card, on the What It Costs reasoning.
