## The archiving pass of 2026-09-23, part 2: the desktop section

The desktop section held 14.6 KB of the brief, most of it per-mechanism build history. What stayed in CLAUDE.md is the rule each mechanism enforces; what follows is the section verbatim as it stood before the pass.

### The desktop section, as it stood before the pass

- **The desktop app is the same code in an Electron window (`desktop/`, since 2026-09-21, 1.0.42.16).** Direct decision: "I would rather have a desktop app instead of a web app or use via a web browser," then "Electron is fine, write it up and start on step 1." Step 1 (the shell and installer) and step 2 (carrying a phone's data over, both directions) are built; step 3 is an Open row in the Project Tracker. **The per-version account of 1.0.42.16 through 1.0.42.29 was archived to `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` on 2026-09-22; read it there before re-deciding anything below.** What stands:
  - **How it is built.** `node desktop/build-web.js` runs `expo export -p web` with `INSIDE_STORY_DESKTOP=1`, which makes `metro.config.js` resolve expo-sqlite, expo-secure-store, expo-notifications and expo-file-system to the stand-ins in `lib/desktop/` and the phone-only natives (speech, Health Connect, zeroconf, static server, OCR) to `unavailableModule.ts`; the 160 MB reference database ships beside the app (`extraResources`) and is copied into the data folder on first run and again after an upgrade changes it. `desktop/main.js` serves the export over a private `app://inside-story/` scheme and does what the natives did: SQLite on Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (no native module, no compiler), secrets through `safeStorage`, reminders as timers raising system notifications, files under `%APPDATA%/inside-story-desktop/`. `preload.js` exposes all of it as `window.insideStoryDesktop`, `lib/desktop/bridge.ts` is the one TypeScript description of that object, and `isDesktopApp()` there is the check the app itself uses. The phone bundle is untouched: the flag is never set for it and `@expo/fingerprint` does not hash `metro.config.js`. `cd desktop && npm run dist` builds `desktop/dist/Inside Story Setup <version>.exe`; `buildVersion` in `electron-builder.yml` carries the four-part version and bumps with the app. Dev helpers on `main.js`: `INSIDE_STORY_LOG=1`, `INSIDE_STORY_SCREENSHOT=<png>`, `INSIDE_STORY_CLICK="label,label"`, `INSIDE_STORY_EVAL="<expression>"`, `INSIDE_STORY_DEV_URL` for Metro; under Git Bash set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or a `/route` becomes a Windows path.
  - **A JS change reaches the desktop only by building and installing a new .exe.** `eas update` carries every JS change to a phone by itself, which is where the finishing ritual used to end, so 1.0.49.4 through 1.0.49.9 all shipped to the phone and none of them reached Windows before it was noticed by hand on 2026-09-22. **`node desktop/check-installer-current.js` belongs in the same pass as `bump_version.js --check`, `tsc` and the audits**: it compares the newest `desktop/dist/Inside Story Setup <version>.exe` against `constants/version.ts` and exits 1 when the repo has moved past it. It reports what was BUILT rather than what is installed, so walking through the installer is still a person’s step.
  - **Two checks that must stay at 0.** `node desktop/check-packaged-files.js` walks every local `require` from `main.js` and `preload.js` against `electron-builder.yml`'s `files:` list, because a module added beside `main.js` is left out of the installer until its line is added (`cloudFolder.js` was, and the installed 1.0.42.25 opened to "Cannot find module './cloudFolder'" while the unpacked shell ran); it runs first in `npm run dist`, `dist:mac` and `pack`. `node desktop/check-collapsed-text.js --menus`, after `node desktop/build-web.js`, asks the running desktop build for any visible text drawn at zero size on every tab and both popup menus: a one-line Text inside a fixed box shrinks to nothing in a browser (flex-shrink 1) where a phone lets it hang past the edge (Yoga, 0), and no static audit can see it.
  - **Layout on a wide window.** `lib/menuFit.ts` owns it: TabHub's card centered on the window (`menuCardLeft`; a phone keeps its left anchor), hub menus spanning the phone width or the desktop window's 480 dp starting width (`hubMenuCardSpan`), corner hubs a fixed distance from TabHub rather than from the corner (`cornerHubLeft`, `secondaryHubCardLeft`), and `PageIdentityLabel` at its starting width (`pageIdentityBoxSpan`). Text size is Chromium page zoom kept by `desktop/zoom.js` (125% by default, Ctrl and + / - / 0, a View menu, a Text size picker in Profile). **The corner box and `VersionLabel` zoom with the artwork and are deliberately NOT pinned against desktop text size**: a 1.0.42.23 pin was undone by direct instruction in 1.0.42.24 ("match how the mobile version is done"). Do not re-add it. On web `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` calls `enableScreens(true)` at module level, without which every visited tab stays drawn under the current one, and a tap on another hub's button while a menu is open lands on that hub through the focus-gated registry in `lib/hubHandoff.ts`.
  - **Phone-only features say so and name the phone**, through `lib/desktop/phoneOnly.ts` (`PhoneOnlyNotice` for a lens or screen, `announcePhoneOnly` for a button, `scripts/test_phone_only.js`): camera, voice, Health Connect, Sync over Wi-Fi, and a picked photo displayed from a `file://` URI. The two file dialogs do work (`desktop/files.js`, `files:pick` and `files:saveAs`): Restore from a File opens a browse window and `shareFileIfAvailable` becomes Save As, so an exported backup, a PDF report and a shared `.is` file land where the person chooses. `Directory.pickDirectoryAsync` still says not available.
  - **On a computer OneDrive is the folder on the disk, and there is no sign-in** (1.0.42.25), because the phone's Graph sign-in ends at a `hashimotosapp://` redirect nothing on a PC is registered for. `lib/oneDriveAuth.ts` reports signed in on desktop and `lib/oneDriveGraph.ts` sends every call to `lib/desktop/cloudFolder.ts`, which addresses a folder as `driveId 'disk'` with the absolute path as its `itemId` in the same `app_meta` row, so nothing in `lib/db.ts`, `lib/syncInbox.ts` or the backup code changed. `desktop/cloudFolder.js` does the file work in the main process, writing to a temp file then renaming so the OneDrive client never uploads half a backup, and refusing a write outside a detected root, the home folder, or a folder picked through the OS dialog this run. **A folder travels between the two kinds of device by its sentence**, "OneDrive / Apps / Inside Story" (`folderFromPhonePath`, `folderFromComputerPath`). The fuller account is in the archive.
  - **One person's two devices stay in step through the shared folder (1.0.42.28 onward).** Each device keeps one encrypted copy of its whole database in the Backups folder (`inside-story-snapshot-<phone|computer>-<fingerprint>.json`, replaced on every save) beside a plaintext record, `inside-story-sync.json`, which says which device saved last and when and carries no health content; manual `inside-story-backup-*` files are untouched. It is turned on in Profile > Backup & Restore with one password, the same on both devices. `lib/snapshotSync.ts` holds every decision with no I/O, `lib/snapshotSyncDevice.ts` reads, writes and restores, `lib/databaseActivity.ts` counts row-changing statements, and `components/SnapshotSyncWatcher.tsx` saves about fifteen seconds after the last write and checks the folder at startup, on foreground, on desktop window focus and every half minute. The time OneDrive takes to carry a file between the two still sits between them. **The per-version account of how this was built, and of the bug behind each of the four rules below, is in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`, and belongs read before re-deciding any of it.** Four things hold, each of which a later session will be tempted to undo:
    1. **Some rows and some tables never travel.** `DEVICE_LOCAL_META_KEYS` in `lib/snapshotSync.ts` lists the `app_meta` rows a device keeps to itself: a save strips them before hashing and a load puts this device's back, so an older snapshot cannot strip them either. **Add a key to that list whenever a new `app_meta` row addresses hardware, a path, a permission or a bundled file, and never assume a row is safe because it looks like a setting**, which is what carrying `onedrive_folder` over taught: the phone inherited the computer's Windows path, could reach no folder, and quietly published nothing for a day. `DEVICE_LOCAL_TABLES` is the same rule for whole tables and holds `sync_change_log`, so each device keeps its account of what happened. A phone holding a folder chosen on a computer adopts it by its sentence (`folderFromComputerPath`), and a folder that cannot be reached is said once per run.
    2. **Every arrival is a three-way merge, record by record** (`lib/snapshotMerge.ts`, which imports nothing): base, here and there, decided per row, so a row only one side touched carries straight over and a row both sides touched is settled by the time the row itself carries (`TIME_COLUMNS`), falling back to whichever device saved later, with the losing change written down as a clash rather than vanishing. The agreed copy is a plain `inside-story-sync-base.json` at `Paths.document`, and missing but clean means what is here IS the agreed copy. Row shapes are read from the schema at merge time (`readSchemaShapes`), so a table added later merges without anybody listing it, and `WORKED_OUT_TABLES` are taken wholesale from the later side, since they are computed rather than recorded. Three corrections stand, each bought with a bug, each accounted for in full in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`: **the agreed copy is what the OTHER device last sent, never what this one published** (1.0.49.11, so `saveSnapshot` calls `seedMergeBase`, which writes only when there is no base at all, while a load takes the base whole and a merge takes what arrived, renumbered into this device's ids by `mergeTables`; the same applies to `peer_sync_base`); **a merge marks the device unsaved only when it has something to send** (1.0.49.10, `sendsBack`, without which two devices left open answered each other every half minute, and which is why the two fold maps moved to the device-local `visual_fold_state`); and **Sync Now never forces**, since forcing would put this device's rows where both devices' rows belong, with `planBeforeSave` looking for a copy to take in BEFORE checking whether anything here is unsaved.
    3. **What changed is said in words, and the words carry no health content out of the encryption.** `lib/snapshotChanges.ts` reduces the stripped tables to one `{n, h}` per table and diffs two stamps into phrases through a map of roughly 50 areas ("3 more meals and edits to your schedule. Not saved here yet: 1 more capture"), where a count comes from one table per area so a salad and its six ingredient rows read as "1 more salad", four phrases at most, then "N other things". **The list rides INSIDE the encrypted snapshot** (a `syncChanges` key), never in the plaintext record, since what somebody added to is as much their health as what they added; the baseline it is diffed against is too big for the Android secure store and lives in `app_meta`, written with the write tracking suspended.
    4. **Nothing is said out loud, and the log is where a merge is read.** Direct instruction, 1.0.49.9: "we have proven the changes work and are reliable. Now we need to turn off the notifications until we see a reason to make them available, how and where." `ANNOUNCE_MERGES` in `lib/snapshotSync.ts` is a constant set to false, read by `lib/snapshotSyncDevice.ts` and `lib/peerSyncDevice.ts`, so one line covers both kinds of merge and turning the notices back on is that one line. It is a constant rather than a changed default because both devices already carry `announce: true`, so a flipped default would have left them talking. Three things still speak: the first-time question, which is why `lib/snapshotChanges.ts` and its tests stay; a folder that cannot be reached, since a sync failing in silence was the 1.0.42.30 bug; and "Save to the Shared Folder Now", which was pressed on purpose. The log is `sync_change_log` plus `lib/syncLog.ts`, read on `app/sync-activity.tsx` and reached from Profile > Backup & Restore, one band per merge with each line naming who did it and marking a clash, grouped so a shopping list with eleven items ticked off is one line. Covered by `scripts/test_snapshot_merge.js` (178), `test_snapshot_sync.js` (87), `test_snapshot_changes.js` (101) and `test_sync_log.js` (25).
  - **1.0.49.4: that same process runs between two people, not only between one person's devices.** Direct instruction: "the communication flow as per what is being done between the user's devices needs to be the same kind of process that happens between partners, and their children, and where applicable, their care giver." The engine is the same engine (`mergeTables`), and everything added on top of it is the boundary. Full account in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`, including the condensed text. What stands: **`lib/peerRelationships.ts` is the inverse of the device rule, an ALLOWLIST**, since two devices hold one database between them while two people hold two and almost nothing belongs to both, so nothing crosses unless a relationship names it and `tablesThatCross()` is that list. Three ways a person can hold something: `shared` (both change it, so it merges), `theirs` (one owns it and the other keeps a copy, so a copy replaces), `onTheirBehalf` (both write and it merges, and the records belong to the other person). An area marked `ready: false` (`schedule`, `meds`, `symptoms`) carries no table at all, so no caller can send it by accident. `lib/peerMerge.ts` refuses and names a whole table outside the list rather than dropping it in silence, and keeps single columns on this phone (`keepsHome`), without which a partner ticking a line off would blank the note underneath it. The payload is filtered through `tablesToSend` on the way OUT, since a privacy decision is either enforced in one place or hoped for in several, and **`talksAutomatically(role)` replaced every `role === 'partner'` transport gate**, so all five carriers reach a child or caregiver link the moment its setting-up ships.
  - The notice and the log are the ones above: `sync_change_log` carries `person_name` and `person_role`, `app/sync-activity.tsx` names the person and the link (`howYouAreLinked`) instead of a device on lines that came from them, and `ANNOUNCE_MERGES` governs both kinds of merge at once. Today the shopping list is the single area that merges between two people (`PARTNER_SHARING_STATE`); conditions and the meal plan still cross as a copy from whoever owns them. Still open: setting up a child or a caregiver link at all.

### The delivery bullet, shortened

- **Delivery: JS ships OTA, native ships by rebuild.** `eas update --branch preview` publishes every JS change and is the last step of every request. **Publish it as `eas update --branch preview --platform android`, never with the platform left off.** Without a platform eas-cli exports all three, and the web export fails on `expo-sqlite`'s `wa-sqlite.wasm` because web only resolves through the desktop stand-ins under `INSIDE_STORY_DESKTOP=1` (`metro.config.js`); nothing consumes a web update anyway, since the desktop app ships as an installer and a JS change reaches Windows only through `node desktop/build-web.js` plus `cd desktop && npm run dist` (see the desktop section's installer check). `eas build --profile preview --platform android` (via `npx --yes eas-cli`, no local install) is only for changes to native code, and forces both phones to reinstall. **Before any rebuild, gather everything rebuild-gated into it.** `runtimeVersion` is a fingerprint; `fingerprint.config.js` skips app.json versions and `.gitignore` so neither drifts the runtime (each was found stranding OTA updates, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-14). The per-build inventory of what 1.0.37.33, 1.0.37.41 and 1.0.37.42 each compiled in, and the dated list of when each of those features was wired up in JS, are in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`. `https://insidestoryapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` is hosted on Cloudflare (Worker `inside-story-site`, deployed from `docs/app-links`, see its README), so the App Link verifies on install, and the same Worker serves landing pages at `/connect` and `/import-shared` for a phone without the app.

## The archiving pass of 2026-09-23, part 3: standing rules, architecture and open next steps

Each rule kept its instruction in CLAUDE.md and lost the account of how it came about. Verbatim as each stood before the pass:

### The audit_ai_isms paragraph

  **This rule is checkable now, so stop checking it by memory.** `node scripts/audit_ai_isms.js [paths]` walks a character-level scanner over `lib`, `app`, `components`, `constants` and `hooks`, separating string literals, JSX text runs, SQL template literals and code comments, and reports hits in 13 categories at two tiers: `block` (fix it) and `look` (a person decides). The categories are the filler words, redundant "own", dashes standing in for punctuation, commentary about the writing instead of the writing, announcing its own honesty, the "not X, it is Y" reversal and its cleft form, the "X is the Y" pronouncement, discourse markers nobody speaks, words nobody says out loud, the summing-up flourish, headline shapes, the hedge pivot, and the rule of three. Run it on anything you wrote before calling content work done. It reported 4,093 hits across 142 files when written, on 2026-09-18, and the whole-app sweep that followed is what brought that down.

### The ai-ism-editor paragraph

  **`.claude/agents/ai-ism-editor.md` is the agent that does the removing.** Direct instruction, 2026-09-18: it runs on newly written or newly changed content only, never on a schedule and never on content nobody asked about, and its start and completion are announced every time. It reports a per-category tally with the before and after text of every change, because the tally is as much the deliverable as the edits. Claude Code reads `.claude/agents/` once, when a session starts, so an agent written during a session is missing from that session. That is what `Agent type 'ai-ism-editor' not found` meant through 1.0.40.1 to 1.0.40.4, each of which was swept by hand plus `scripts/audit_ai_isms.js` instead. The definition is valid and needs no editing; the fix is to restart Claude Code, and never to substitute a different agent, since the standing rule everywhere else is no subagents on this project.

### Standing consequence 1, Digest titles

  1. **A Digest title says what the entry is about.** Direct instruction: "The title of something shouldn't make someone still wonder what they are about to read." The shape that was removed is a subject, a colon, and a phrase that promises rather than states ("Water: The One Nutrient With No Official Government Recommendation at All"). 116 titles were rewritten to name the subject and the finding. The colon-subtitle convention was explicitly rejected as house style, so do not reintroduce it, and do not write a new entry with one.

### Standing consequence 3, cross-reference refrain

  3. **The "already covered" cross-reference refrain is out of customer-facing text.** A bare self-reference ("already covered in this category") was deleted outright, since it points at nothing a reader can go to. A pointer naming a place a reader can actually reach was kept, minus the word "already", which presumes the reader has been through it. 27 instances survive entirely in code comments, which is where curation rationale belongs.

### The version-bump rule

- **Bump the version by running `node scripts/bump_version.js`, once per distinct request the user provides, not once per file changed.** Direct instruction, 2026-08-23: "It isn't per change because there may be many changes that happen at once, but each time I provide something for you to do or to change, there needs to be an increment for that day." Format is `1.0.DAY.UPDATE`, and **DAY is which day of work it is, so it increments the moment the calendar date changes and UPDATE goes back to 1**: direct correction, 2026-09-22, "Once midnight happens, it is the next day ... It absolutely never should ever continue with version numbering from the previous day of work." Hand-typing it drifted seven days behind over three weeks, which is why the script exists and why nobody edits the four files by hand: it counts the distinct commit days out of git, works out whether this is a new day, and writes `constants/version.ts`, `app.json`, `package.json` and `desktop/electron-builder.yml` together. `node scripts/bump_version.js --check` exits 1 when the day is stale, and belongs in the same pass as `tsc`, the audits and the push. Treat the bump the same as git push and the Notion sync, part of finishing work rather than a separate ask.

### The databases-out-of-git rule

- **Neither SQLite database is in git, and neither goes back in.** Since 2026-09-21, after GitHub's warning that the account had used 90% of its 10 GiB of Git LFS storage. Both files had been LFS-tracked, and every commit of `assets/data/foods_reference.db` (161 MB) or `unified-database/unified_foods.sqlite` (115 MB) uploaded a whole new object that GitHub keeps for good. Removing a file from git reclaims nothing; only deleting and recreating the repository does, which is a separate decision. What holds now: both paths are in `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` keeps its LFS lines so a re-add could never land as a plain 161 MB blob, EAS still uploads both for a build because `.easignore` does not exclude them, and `node scripts/backup_reference_dbs.js` copies them to `C:\Users\TonyR\OneDrive\Desktop\AppProject\_backups\reference-dbs\` under fixed names (OneDrive's version history keeps the older ones). **Run that script whenever either database changes, as part of finishing the work, the same as the version bump and the push.** A fresh clone has no database until it is copied back from that folder.

### The no-bare-text rule

- **No text ever sits directly on a tab's photographic background without a surface of its own.** Direct instruction, 2026-08-29: "No font should ever be directly on the tab background without its own background anywhere in the app." Three remedies, in order of preference: (1) a heading labelling ONE card moves INSIDE that card as its first row; (2) a heading introducing a GROUP of cards, or a standalone empty, error, loading or footnote line, gets a surface of its own (`groupHeadingChip`/`panelStandalone`, defined per screen); (3) an outline-only control gets a fill, since its label is otherwise sitting on the photo. Prefer giving the surface to the shared CONTAINER over chipping each line, so related text reads as one block rather than several stacked boxes. **`scripts/audit_bare_text_on_background.js` and `scripts/audit_dark_text_shadow.js` are the checks and both must stay at 0**, the second added 2026-09-21 after "any font that is black ... looks like a smudged font" on both the phone and Windows; a dark colour on a shadowed shared style is overridden with `textShadowColor: 'transparent', textShadowRadius: 0` rather than by splitting the style. `scripts/add_style_background.js` and `scripts/wrap_bare_text_lines.js` apply fixes at scale. Full account in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`.

### The edge-measurement rule

- **Anything anchored to an edge is measured against the window, not against a number somebody typed.** Direct request, 2026-09-18, following the two-classes-of-text rule above, which fixed how tall the popup menus WANT to be and never asked whether the screen is that tall. It was not: `LensHub` at Normal spacing already wanted 402 dp against a 411 dp landscape phone. `useWindowDimensions()` reports dp rather than pixels, so **one measurement covers every case at once**, and there are four of them: Android's **Display size** setting (which raises the density, so the same screen reports 1.1x to 1.3x fewer dp, and which needs no second device and no rotation, making it the one most people will actually hit), a **landscape or split-screen viewport**, a **foldable**, and an **Android 16+ large screen**, which ignores an app's orientation lock outright. `app.json` sets `"orientation": "portrait"`, which narrows who sees a short viewport and does not remove it, since `"supportsTablet": true` is set too.

### The menuFit bullet

  - The arithmetic lives in `lib/menuFit.ts` (`menuCardRoom`, `fitMenuCard`), pure and with no React in it, so `node scripts/test_menuFit.js` can check it without a phone, and `useMenuCardFit(desired, minHeight)` in `constants/floatingButton.ts` is the hook every menu calls, since that file already owns where each hub sits. **A clamped card scrolls**: all three menus put their content through a `ScrollView` unconditionally, because a `ScrollView` whose content is shorter than its frame simply does not scroll, so there is one code path to be right about rather than two. `node scripts/audit_menu_card_fit.js` is the check and must stay at 0: it requires every menu file to call `useMenuCardFit`, and rejects a hand-typed `height`, `maxHeight` or `minHeight` on any `card*` style in one. `PageIdentityLabel` was checked and deliberately not changed, since it is pinned to the bottom edge and asks for less window than it is given; the menus overflowed because they are tall and grow upward.

### The Tell Claude lead

- **There may be notes waiting for you, and reading them is part of starting a session (Tell Claude, 1.0.49.8, 2026-09-22).** Direct request: a long press on any fold band (one edit, in `components/TabBand.tsx`, which every lens band passes through) leaves a note about that band, so a band holding a form with six steps is one note covering all six; a button against the left edge covers Home, where a long press is already the rearrange gesture, and the Windows app. A note fills in its device, the version, and the tab, lens and band by itself (`components/PageIdentityLabel.tsx` gained a `useEffect` reporter and nothing else, so the pinned corner box is unchanged).

### The Tell Claude queueing bullet

  - **A note is queued, never applied.** Nothing on a device changes what the app says: the note carries the wording as it stood, the source gets changed, and the change ships, so no phone can disagree with the repo. **On finding notes waiting, do the clear ones and report them, and bring an observation or an ambiguous one back first.** It is off by default and it is for building this app: the switch lives in Profile > Developer Tools, a card gated on `__DEV__ || Updates.channel === 'preview'` that renders nothing at all in a store release. `dev_notes` travels between one person's two devices, raises no change phrase in `lib/snapshotChanges.ts`, and can never reach another person, since `lib/peerRelationships.ts` is an allowlist. A note carries no screenshot: `react-native-view-shot` is a native module and would force a rebuild.

### The multi-device sync design paragraph

**Multi-device sync model, as designed:** the encrypted cloud snapshot is the current state rather than just a backup, pulled and decrypted locally, worked against fully offline, and pushed back. Three layered mechanisms were designed against concurrent edits (an exclusive lock held by the first device to pull and recorded in cloud metadata, an active takeover by a visible tap-required push rather than a silent one, which both mobile OSes throttle unreliably, and a hard 30-minute lease so an unreachable device can never lock somebody out), with last-write-wins plus a visible activity log underneath all three, deliberately not a CRDT, a choice validated by AnkiWeb's mature sync falling back to one-way overwrite when changes cannot merge. **What shipped instead, from 1.0.42.28, is the shared-folder snapshot sync described in the Technology stack section above, which merges three ways rather than locking.** The locking design is kept in full in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`, and is the step nobody has needed yet.

### The security prerequisite list

**Ordered prerequisite list for the security work** (given directly 2026-08-15; the full seven-step list with the reasoning behind each step's place in the order is in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`). Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are built, confirmed by reading the code on 2026-09-06: `tweetnacl` is a dependency, `lib/deviceIdentity.ts` keeps a private key in `expo-secure-store` (Android Keystore, iOS Keychain), `connections` stores a unique public key per person, and `decodeShareEnvelope` in `lib/sharing.ts` verifies every received payload against the verbatim signed bytes, rejecting outright on mismatch. Step 4, the invitation and pairing exchange, was one-sided and became two-way in 1.0.34.30. Step 6, `.is` OS-level file-type registration, is in `app.json`'s intent filters (content:// and file:// `.is` paths, plus the https App Link added 2026-09-14). **Step 7, extending past recipes to gardening, exercise and the rest, is still open, alongside transport**, and should be designed and built together with tier-separation work rather than as a phase beforehand.

Named directly as still open: Today's Advisories (a different real mechanism, today's actual logged meals against the interaction-rules engine, not audited); and whether the Food builders' own embedded `FoodLookup` instances should ever gain the same "For You" card, a deliberate scoping decision this pass made, not something to silently extend without asking, since builders already carry their own separate live per-ingredient advisory and full pre-save depth report.

The rule settled first, which every outside request follows: (1) a keyed lookup, a barcode or product name in and a label out, routed through the `inside-story-site` Worker off a D1 snapshot with the edge cache in front, so only the key leaves the phone; (2) anything keyed by condition, pre-fetched by the Worker for all 19 on a schedule and downloaded as a whole bundle, so a device never makes a per-condition request; (3) anything keyed by location, coarsened to a rounded coordinate or a city and never the precise fix, stated in-product the way the voice boundary is stated, and opt-in. 28. **The daily-living program for the second audience, eleven Project Tracker rows written 2026-09-16.** Follows from the "Who it is for" section above: somebody whose reason for opening this app is that daily life will not stay in their head. Nine Open Feature rows, one Deferred Feature row and one Deferred Decision row, so read those rather than re-deriving any of it; the eleven are also listed in the archive, in the agreed order of value for the effort. Three things a stale assessment will claim are missing and are not: meal and hydration reminders (1.0.39.3), the sensory and regulation check-in tags (1.0.39.3), and Low Stimulation (1.0.39.4, on Home since 1.0.39.6). As of 1.0.50.6 the capture inbox, the dated reminders, the lead times, Routines, Did I Do It, both Days Until cards and "where did I put it" all reach Home, and Trends > Keeping Up (1.0.50.8) is how any of it is going. **Simple View plus one clear next thing on Home** is the one piece of the list that is not built at all, alongside the two deferred rows: **a way in that does not require a condition**, which decides whether any of the rest is ever seen and needs the Free tier line re-drawn deliberately, and **whether ADHD and autism become selectable profiles**, deferred on how to give them framing and check-in tags without the condition scoring implying that diet treats them.

### The free viewer companion bullet

- *Free viewer companion.* Reads periodic snapshots from a natively-shared cloud folder, modeled on Anki shared decks (one-way periodic reimport, no live subscription). Sees meal schedule, shopping list, and trend reports. One narrow write exception: **checking off shopping-list items** and marking scheduled tasks done. These are idempotent, single-field, low-conflict actions sent back as a small delta file, needing no merge logic.

### The reminders paragraph

**Reminders and scheduling: contextual from day one, not clock-based.** "Take your levothyroxine" should account for what's actually been logged, since a calcium-rich food earlier pushes the safe window later. Two mechanisms: fully local on-device scheduled notifications for anything self-contained, and a minimal **content-blind** push relay (APNs/FCM) purely for cross-device wake-up signals, never carrying health content. Background execution is throttled on both mobile OSes, so instant recomputation is only guaranteed in the foreground. Design around that. Reminders should show their own freshness ("based on food logged as of 7:45am"), because a confidently-wrong contextual reminder is worse than an honestly-uninformed static one.

### The late logging paragraph

**Late and retroactive logging** must be low-friction: guided quick-select (what did you eat, pick from favorites or recents, when did it happen, smart time picker), never a blank form. Every late entry immediately shows its consequence (recalculated schedule impact), turning logging into a teaching moment. Scheduled reminders double as catch-up checkpoints.

### The reporting paragraph

**Reporting.** Doctor, nutritionist, trainer, and self reports are different views over the same timestamped, taggable log data, with every entry timestamped and taggable from the start so reporting is a query rather than a rebuild. Reports generate entirely on-device (PDF export, no server rendering), consistent with the privacy model. The laid-out PDF export shipped 2026-09-14 (1.0.37.37): one `ReportDocument` rendered two ways, plain text on screen and HTML through `expo-print` for the PDF, shared through `expo-sharing`. Doctor, nutritionist, trainer and self views over that document are not yet separate; there is one Overview report.

### The .is format paragraph

**Sharing between people: the `.is` format.** `.is` is intended as the one general-purpose file format for anything shareable: recipes and favorites (built), plus future gardening, exercise, and other non-health content. A person's health domain stays outside it, since that's the tier model's job. Build the payload shape generically from day one (an envelope type per content kind), not recipe-specific.

### The evidence honesty paragraph

**Evidence honesty.** Of the supplied sources, exactly one claim carries strong trial-level evidence: selenium reducing TPO antibodies, backed by a meta-analysis of 21 RCTs. Everything else is practitioner framework, case report, or survey data. The thiamine claim is a **3-patient case report**, not the "landmark clinical pilot trial" it was described as; gluten, dairy, and soy trigger rankings come from one practitioner's self-reported audience survey; and the staging framework itself is its own author explaining it. That is fine to build on **provided the app labels it honestly.** The full source table with per-claim tiers is in the archive.

### The unified database status paragraph

**Status (this drifts, so verify via `sqlite3.exe unified_foods.sqlite` rather than trusting these numbers):** all 9 sources ingested, classified, and matched. 32,707 raw records, of which 16,661 are classified whole-food, 13,093 are not, and 2,953 are unresolved. 14,521 match groups. The audit tool is live at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/51c33d40-cbd9-4468-90b0-e1e460fd5b1d, and review has started (242 classification decisions applied) but is nowhere near complete.

## The archiving pass of 2026-09-23, part 5: the last of the standing rules

Each of these kept its instruction in CLAUDE.md and lost the elaboration around it. Verbatim as it stood before the pass:

### The Rule Engine lead paragraph

- **The Rule Engine, a standing name for a real, recurring gap.** Direct request, 2026-08-26, after the oxalate/calcium-pairing work below: "we need a word for this part of the app so we both know what we are talking about... it has to always apply to all of the ways the information needs to be wired up, so nothing ever gets left out." **The Rule Engine is every mechanism in this app that encodes one real, evidence-based nutrition or health fact as a reusable "if X then Y" rule about a food, ingredient, nutrient, or combination**, as opposed to the Digest's own long-form narrative writing. It is not one file or one table; it is a set of real, already-built pieces that all have to be checked whenever a genuinely new fact enters the app:

### The audit_ai_isms paragraph, second pass

  **This rule is checkable now, so stop checking it by memory.** `node scripts/audit_ai_isms.js [paths]` walks a character-level scanner over `lib`, `app`, `components`, `constants` and `hooks`, separating string literals, JSX text runs, SQL template literals and code comments, and reports hits in 13 categories at two tiers: `block` (fix it) and `look` (a person decides). The categories are listed in the script. Run it on anything you wrote before calling content work done. It reported 4,093 hits across 142 files when written, on 2026-09-18, and the whole-app sweep that followed is what brought that down.

### The ai-ism-editor paragraph

  **`.claude/agents/ai-ism-editor.md` is the agent that does the removing.** Direct instruction, 2026-09-18: it runs on newly written or newly changed content only, never on a schedule and never on content nobody asked about, and its start and completion are announced every time. It reports a per-category tally with the before and after text of every change, because the tally is as much the deliverable as the edits. Claude Code reads `.claude/agents/` once, when a session starts, so an agent written during a session is missing from that session. `Agent type 'ai-ism-editor' not found` means restart Claude Code, and never substitute a different agent, since the standing rule everywhere else is no subagents on this project.

### The shelf-subdivision item of the Digest pattern rule

  1. **Never leave a shelf covering more than one subject undivided.** Run the real count for the shelf being added to. Past roughly 12 entries it needs named subgroups (`CONDITION_TOPIC_SUBGROUPS`, which since 2026-08-29 works for EVERY category, not just conditions: Earth Matters and Home Gardening route through `applyConditionTopicSubgroups` too, and its topic key is a plain string). Design the split from the actual entry titles, never arbitrarily, and verify programmatically that every id is accounted for.

### The FURNITURE class of text

  2. **FURNITURE is the app's own structure**: the two popup menus (`TabHub`, `LensHub`, `MyItemsHub`), the corner box that says where you are, the version number. It is positioned rather than flowing, so it cannot grow without landing on its neighbour. Its room is BUDGETED from both inputs at once, the app's line spacing setting and the phone's font-size setting, through `menuLineHeight` and `menuLineBudget` in `constants/typography.ts`. A label's line height and the row height budgeted for it come from the same function, which is the part that stops this class of bug recurring: a hand-typed 13 next to a real 18 is exactly how the TabHub bug was written. Every label in a menu carries `maxFontSizeMultiplier={MENU_MAX_FONT_SCALE}`, and the card measures itself against that same cap through `useWindowDimensions().fontScale`, which re-renders when the setting changes where a module constant read once cannot.

### The audit_chrome_font_scale paragraph

  `node scripts/audit_chrome_font_scale.js` is the check and must stay at 0. It walks the real TypeScript AST over the five furniture files, per-file in `cap` or `pin` mode, skips a Text nested in a Text (which inherits both attributes), and holds a `READING_TEXT_IN_CHROME` allowlist where each entry needs a written reason naming what that text grows into. Run it beside `audit_bare_text_on_background.js` before calling UI work done. Changing either line spacing or letter spacing still restarts the app, because `constants/typography.ts` applies both once at module load and every screen runs `StyleSheet.create` at import time.

### The open-lists rule

- **Lists are open-ended, and removing an entry never orphans or destroys a record.** Direct instruction, 2026-09-20: "we need to make it as future-proof as possible by giving ways to add things in lists that we haven't foreseen the need for, or the existence of," and, on removal, "I don't think anything should be orphaned if the user deletes a field label they created. That isn't good database management." Two halves. (1) Any picker over a fixed list of kinds, spaces, categories or labels gets an "Add a ... of your own" entry: a sentinel option, a one-line form in place, Rename and Remove for the person's entries only, dedupe by lowercased name. A new open list needs no table of its own, since `garden_custom_terms` holds any list keyed by name and `components/GardenTermField.tsx` is the picker with the add, rename and move-first removal built in; `garden_cost_kinds` and `garden_spaces` (shared `GardenSpaceField`) are the older per-table precedents. (2) Removing an entry that records read: things in use move to a replacement the person picks first, things with history are retired rather than deleted and stay readable as documentation (`garden_spaces.retired_at`), and a row is deleted outright only when nothing refers to it. **Never fall back to a catch-all like Something else, never NULL a column, never cascade.** The same applies to the things themselves: a garden area with anything recorded under it moves to Past Areas (`archived_at`) only once every grow in it has finished, and `deleteGardenPlot` refuses while anything is recorded under it. Decision logic lives in pure modules (`planSpaceRemoval` in `lib/gardenSpaces.ts`, `pastAreaBlocker` in `lib/gardenAreaLifecycle.ts`, `planTermRemoval` in `lib/growSetup.ts`) so the test scripts cover it without a phone. **Chooser lists of names read alphabetically** (direct instruction, 2026-09-21): `sortByLabel` in `lib/choiceOrder.ts` sorts by label, case-insensitively, with the person's entries merged in among the built-ins rather than appended, a fixed entry (Unassigned, Something else, the add-your-own sentinel) held at its end by the caller, and a list that is a scale left in its natural order. Build a new name list through it.

### The no-long-shelf rule

- **No topic renders as one long, undifferentiated horizontal shelf once it grows past roughly a dozen entries.** Direct instruction, 2026-08-25: "There should be groups of information that is specific to one diet or eating style or another, rather than one continuous scrolling left to right list of them," confirmed the same day to mean literally throughout the Digest: "Everything must have continuity throughout the Digest." Basic Health topics get real `subtopics` (the `BasicHealthTopic.subtopics` mechanism Essential Nutrients established); an oversized condition topic gets an entry in `CONDITION_TOPIC_SUBGROUPS`, keyed by `entry.category` and the `ConditionTopic` name, hooked into `groupConditionEntries` (`purple-digest.tsx`). Both mechanisms group by whatever distinguishes that shelf's entries, verified programmatically against the corpus before shipping (every id accounted for, none dropped or duplicated), never an arbitrary split. Applied 2026-08-25 to 7 Basic Health topics and 18 (condition, topic) pairs across 13 conditions. Most remaining topics are small enough (2 to 10 entries) that this does not apply; check real counts before assuming one needs it.

## The reward design for the freed tab screens, 2026-09-24

Written the day 1.0.51.1 emptied the tab screen bodies. Asked directly: "what ideas do you have related to how to use the individual tab screen backgrounds? How can they be rewarded for the use, what should they see, what will motivate them to keep inputting data?" This is the design conversation that follows the emptying, recorded because nothing here is built and a later session will otherwise re-derive it or, worse, reach for the version of this that fails.

**Nothing below is approved for building.** One question is still open at the end and it changes every query underneath, so it gets settled before code.

### The decision that shapes everything else

**What grows is made out of the person's records, not awarded for them.** A badge is a token handed over for behaviour. A picture assembled from what somebody actually recorded is a record of their life. Three consequences, each of which is why this shape was picked over the obvious one:

1. It can never be taken away, so there is no loss state and nothing to protect.
2. It needs no praise language, so it clears the no-scoring rule without trying. `scripts/test_keeping_up.js` forbids "well done", "good job" and "keep it up" alongside "you failed" and "slacking", which means praise is banned as squarely as blame. Any design whose point is to congratulate somebody is already outside the rules this app enforces on itself.
3. When somebody logs nothing for three weeks it simply does not grow. It does not wilt, reset or comment. That is the gap-not-zero rule (every periodic figure is `number | null`, a blank period says so in words) applied to a picture instead of a chart.

Every alternative considered contradicted one of the three. A streak breaks, which is a loss state and the documented reason people quit health apps. A level or a point total is a score. A percentage complete implies a finish line somebody is behind.

### What each tab's canvas could be made of

Drawn from that tab's tables, in that tab's colour from `constants/tabs.ts`:

- **Garden** writes itself: plants from the plantings recorded, at the stage each has reached, fruit from the harvests logged, a Past Area's plants drawn back rather than erased.
- **Food** is a table or pantry that fills with one item per DISTINCT whole food ever logged. This is the strongest of the nine, because dietary variety is itself the gut-healing goal, so the picture is a picture of microbiome diversity rather than a prize for app use.
- **Life** is the second audience's tab and has no criteria at all today. A room that furnishes itself as routines run, upkeep gets done, captures get sorted and counters land. The metaphor restates the promise to that audience: this is the outside place holding the details.
- **Signals** must not grow with symptom count, or the app rewards being sick. Stars for check-ins, never for what was in them.
- **Schedules** fills a day arc with meals and doses actually placed.
- **Insights** gains something per pattern found and per food looked up.
- **Trends** and **Reports** read rather than record, so they may deserve span of time covered rather than growth, or nothing.
- **Home** has no gated background (it is the shared canvas mounted once in `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`), so it is outside this entirely.

### Three layers, and only one of them is decoration

Decoration alone will not sustain logging. It buys a novelty bump and then nothing, which is the failure mode of every health app that tried gamification.

1. **The canvas.** Ambient. Never asks for anything, never announces itself, never sends a notification. The moment it says "your vine grew" it has become the app begging for data, which is the manipulative pattern and is out.
2. **Proximity to an answer.** This is the motivator, and probably the whole thing. Not "you broke your streak" but "Pattern Finder needs four more meals logged alongside a symptom before it can say anything about dairy." It is a statement about what the analysis requires, never about the person's virtue, so it is honest and it clears every rule. The machinery exists; the app has never said how close it is.
3. **The payoff.** The moment it says something true about somebody's body that they did not know. That is the core purpose, and the only durable reason anybody logs anything.

### Five constraints to build against

1. **No animation.** The AnimatedSky came out on 2026-08-17 for confirmed battery drain. This thing would be mounted behind every tab, always. Static, composed on focus, or that bug repeats at nine times the scale.
2. **It must be findable when the background is off or personal.** Direct instruction, the same day: "the achievements continue to build themselves so if the user decides to look, they can." So the growth is a layer over whatever background is set, plus one place that shows the whole thing regardless. Default it on for Photo and Generic, off for a photo somebody added, since they chose that photo to be looked at. Low Stimulation turns it off with everything else.
3. **Elapsed time earns some of it, not only volume.** Somebody who logs lightly for a year should have a substantial canvas. Otherwise "more logging" quietly becomes "better person", which is scoring wearing a costume.
4. **Nothing ever regresses.** A gap pauses growth and never reverses it.
5. **Day one must not look broken.** Start it as a season rather than an empty frame, so a new canvas reads as early rather than as failure.

### Badges, in the one form that is allowed

A badge is acceptable as a named fact that stays ("logged something in all twelve builders") and not as a rank. The 30 criteria already in `lib/achievementCriteria.ts` are written the first way, which is the precedent to follow.

### Ruled out explicitly

No numbers on the background (points, counts, percentages). No notification about growth. No leaderboard and no comparison against another person, ever. No loss state of any kind.

### What already exists, so none of it gets rebuilt

`lib/achievementCriteria.ts` is Phase 1 of the header growth vine and Timeline plan (2026-08-21), built deliberately before the vine. 30 criteria, all Tier 1, each backed by an `existsQuery` over a table that exists for its own ordinary reason, each carrying a `tab` the plan earmarks for Phase 2's leaf colour. Storage is `achievement_criteria_progress` in `lib/db.ts`, with `getAchievedCriteriaKeys` and `recordAchievementCriterionMet` as the accessors. Tier 2 (screen-open criteria) needs a usage table and is Phase 7.

**The registry is lopsided, and that is the first piece of work whatever shape wins.** Counted 2026-09-24: Food 17, Schedules 6, Insights 5, Signals 1, Garden 1. **Home, Trends, Reports and Life have none at all.** Life having none is the sharpest gap, since it is the tab the second audience lives on.

### The open question

**Variety or volume?** Does the Food canvas grow from how many DIFFERENT foods have been logged, or from how many times logging happened? The recommendation on the table is variety plus elapsed time, because variety is the gut-healing goal and repetition rewards grinding. Not settled, and it changes every query underneath, so it gets answered before anything is written.

(2) Removing an entry that records read: things in use move to a replacement the person picks first, things with history are retired rather than deleted and stay readable as documentation (`garden_spaces.retired_at`), and a row is deleted outright only when nothing refers to it. **Never fall back to a catch-all like Something else, never NULL a column, never cascade.** The same applies to the things themselves: a garden area with anything recorded under it moves to Past Areas (`archived_at`) only once every grow in it has finished, and `deleteGardenPlot` refuses while anything is recorded under it. Build a new name list through it.

### The Tell Claude rule

- **There may be notes waiting for you, and reading them is part of starting a session (Tell Claude, 1.0.49.8, 2026-09-22).** Direct request: a long press on any fold band (one edit, in `components/TabBand.tsx`, which every lens band passes through) leaves a note about that band, so a band holding a form with six steps is one note covering all six; a button against the left edge covers Home, where a long press is already the rearrange gesture, and the Windows app. A note fills in its device, the version, and the tab, lens and band by itself.
  - **Where to read them: `inside-story-notes.jsonl` in the Backups folder**, which on this PC is a plain file on the disk, so `cat` it. One JSON object per line, a note or a status. **Write an answer back as a new status line rather than editing anything**, since a repeated id is settled by taking the later line, which is what makes the file safe to append to from two devices at once. `lib/devNotes.ts` holds the shape and every sentence with no I/O, `lib/devNotesDb.ts` the table and the file, `lib/tellClaude.ts` how a long press reaches the sheet, `components/TellClaudeHost.tsx` the button and the sheet.
  - **A note is queued, and a wording edit is previewed (1.0.51.12).** The button offers **Edit wording**, which underlines every piece of text; a tap opens a small editor with those words, placed so they stay in sight, and saving writes a `wording` note carrying `originalText` and `newText`. That edit shows at once **on that device only** (Profile > Developer Tools, "Show my wording edits before they ship", on by default), and drops away once its note is marked done, so the shipped source is still the only thing anybody else sees. The mechanism: `metro.config.js` hands the app's own folders `components/reactNativeWithEditableText.js` in place of `react-native`, which is React Native with `Text` swapped for `components/EditableText.tsx`; libraries in `node_modules` are untouched, the outermost Text owns the sentence, and while the switch is off it renders plain React Native Text. **The swap's own files never import the bare name `react-native`**: Metro caches a bare name once for every file outside `node_modules`, so excluding a file by path does nothing, and 1.0.51.12 closed on launch when `EditableText` got the swap back. They go through `components/reactNativeText.js` (`react-native/index`), whose `.web.js` half asks for `react-native-web/dist/exports/Text/index` for the same reason (the cache is per origin folder, and 1.0.52.3 opened to a black screen on Windows when it asked for the swapped path), and `node scripts/test_editable_text_resolver.js` checks an Android export's module graph for it, `--web` the desktop export's. State in `lib/wordingEdits.ts`, which edits count in `editsFromNotes` (`lib/devNotes.ts`). **When acting on one, change the source text named in `originalText`, then mark the note done.** **On finding notes waiting, do the clear ones and report them, and bring an observation or an ambiguous one back first.** It is off by default: the switch lives in Profile > Developer Tools, a card gated on `__DEV__ || Updates.channel === 'preview'` that renders nothing in a store release. `dev_notes` travels between one person's two devices, raises no change phrase in `lib/snapshotChanges.ts`, and can never reach another person, since `lib/peerRelationships.ts` is an allowlist. A note carries no screenshot: `react-native-view-shot` is a native module and would force a rebuild.

### Growing conditions as a record

**Growing conditions as a record, and the sensor plan behind it (2026-09-23, 1.0.50.12).** The idea a later session will be tempted to skip past: **separate the reading from the radio.** A soil moisture figure is worth the same whether it arrived over WiFi or came off a $12 meter, so the record gets built first and every way of filling it is a later, optional addition. Four stages were proposed and **only stage 0 is approved and built**: stage 1 is DIY LAN sensors over the zeroconf and static-server code already compiled in, stage 2 cameras over RTSP or ONVIF (a native module and a rebuild), stage 3 commercial cloud accounts over OAuth. Three corrections to the outside advice that started this bind whatever gets built later: **no time-series database**, since SQLite handles a sensor's rate and a second engine breaks local-first; **no Flutter and no Node or Python backend**, since Expo is settled and a backend is the one thing this app deliberately lacks; and **nothing is built on Home Assistant**, since requiring a hub disqualifies the audience. The phone is the hub.

Stage 0 is `garden_readings`, append-only on the `harvest_uses` precedent, with no foreign key, `plot_name` on the row so a Past Area keeps its readings readable, and a `source` of `hand` or `device` that exists now so stage 1 needs no migration. `measurement_kind` is the fifth open list and the first that is not movable: readings are history, so a measurement name with readings against it retires rather than asking for a reassignment. **Units are turned into one another only where the two mean the same quantity** (°C and °F, mm and in, L and gal, mS/cm and µS/cm); a moisture percentage and a tensiometer centibar are deliberately not a family, nor are lux and PPFD, so readings in the odd unit out are set aside with a line saying how many and in what. Rain and water given are added up over a month, everything else averaged with its lowest and highest, since an average soil temperature hides the night that dropped below freezing. Garden > Growing Conditions is the ninth Garden lens and where a reading goes in; Trends > Growing Conditions is the fifteenth Trends lens and reads only (`lib/growingConditions.ts`, `lib/growingConditionsDb.ts`). The forbidden-words sweep in `scripts/test_growing_conditions.js` adds "too low", "too high", "ideal", "optimal" and "healthy range", since a conditions figure is the easiest place in this app to start telling somebody their soil is wrong.

### Your Story

**Your Story, the guided way through the app (2026-09-24, 1.0.51.4).** The person's use of the app is told as their paper, part book and part newspaper: a heading that reads "Your Story Begins Here", then "Your first edition is taking shape", then "Your Story Continues". The first edition is six sections (Front Page, which is What Matters to You; The Archive; On the Record; The Calendar; The Daily Report; The Inside Story), and each part of life chosen on the Front Page adds one section after them. Every definition and sentence is in `lib/yourStory.ts`, the records it reads in `lib/yourStoryDb.ts` (tables `user_beats` and `your_story_items`), the layout in `components/YourStorySection.tsx`, covered by `scripts/test_your_story.js`. It lives on a Home card, a full page (`app/your-story.tsx`), a Profile entry, a "Where this fits in Your Story" line at the foot of every help sheet, and the empty states of Pattern Finder, Trends and Reports (`components/YourStoryMissingLine.tsx`). Rules that hold: **an item is done when its record exists**, carries the date it went in, and reopens saying so if the record goes; no "step N of M", no percentage, no praise, no blame, no cause claimed; every item links to the exact tab and lens. **Two written exceptions to standing rules:** the nine parts of life (Health, Food, Movement, Home, Garden, Money, Routines, Work, Family, asked as "What parts of your life do you want Inside Story to follow?", and never called beats on screen) are a CLOSED list with no add-your-own, because each one switches on a section somebody has to have written, and choosing never hides anything anywhere; and the Home card can be collapsed and moved but **not turned off** (`HOME_SECTIONS_ALWAYS_SHOWN` in `lib/visualPreferences.ts`), since it is how somebody finds their way back to a step that dropped off. The chosen parts of life travel between one person's devices; `backup_last_saved` does not. It is not a second welcome overlay. **Since 1.0.52.3 it also reads by tab** (`lib/yourStoryTabs.ts`): every tab except Home is listed in two groups, where records go in (Life, Schedules, Signals, Food, Garden) and what records give back (Insights, Trends, Reports), each saying what it gives and, when a record from another tab has to exist first, naming it and going there; one Start here marker once the before-anything items (parts of life, about you, backup) are done. It reads `view.allItems` and never decides doneness itself. **Since 1.0.52.5 it opens as an interview** (direct instruction, 2026-09-25: "Configure this sort of like the app answering interview questions"): conditions, neurodivergence (listing one changes no food score), parts of life, where the person wants to start, meds and supplements, the stage of each staged condition, and eating style with each style explained, one question at a time in `lib/yourStoryInterview.ts` (answers in `your_story_answers`, `lib/yourStoryInterviewDb.ts`, `components/YourStoryInterview.tsx`). After it, `components/YourStoryTour.tsx` says what each WHOLE tab is for, its lenses in named groups, then how to get started, the chosen tab first; `buildTabGuide(view, startPath)` honours that choice. **Since 1.0.52.6 each tab in the tour describes the whole tab, never one feature of it** (direct instruction: "Life is not just about a routine ... What does the Life tab actually do for you? ... What things can the user rely on it to be and do for them?"): what it does for you, a "What you can count on it for" list (`relyOn`), every lens as a compact row with one line saying what it does (`TOUR_LENS_LINES`, `lensLine`), and "The fastest way in", steps ordered so each makes the next more useful, each carrying its `why`, the first not yet done marked Start with this. `scripts/test_your_story.js` fails if a tab gains a lens the tour does not list, or a lens or step lacks its line. **The inputs-to-outputs map at https://claude.ai/artifact/NpNnv37hYpHvz4RGcawXPn is built (1.0.52.7)**: all 22 lenses the owner marked Build, nine on Trends (`lib/trendsMore.ts`), six on Insights (`lib/insightsMore.ts`), each a pure builder handing a `ReadingView` (`lib/readingBands.ts`) to `components/ReadingBandsView.tsx` with its reads in the matching `*Db.ts`, and seven reports (`lib/reportKinds.ts`). `scripts/test_output_lenses.js` runs every builder on sample rows and on nothing and sweeps each sentence against `READING_FORBIDDEN_WORDS`; a new builder goes in it.

### Sync between two people

  - **1.0.49.4: that same process runs between two people, not only between one person's devices.** Direct instruction: "the communication flow as per what is being done between the user's devices needs to be the same kind of process that happens between partners, and their children, and where applicable, their care giver." The engine is the same engine (`mergeTables`), and everything added on top of it is the boundary. **`lib/peerRelationships.ts` is the inverse of the device rule, an ALLOWLIST**, since two devices hold one database between them while two people hold two and almost nothing belongs to both: nothing crosses unless a relationship names it. Three ways a person can hold something: `shared` (merges), `theirs` (a copy replaces), `onTheirBehalf` (merges, and the records belong to the other person). An area marked `ready: false` (`schedule`, `meds`, `symptoms`) carries no table at all. `lib/peerMerge.ts` refuses and names a whole table outside the list rather than dropping it in silence, and keeps single columns on this phone (`keepsHome`). The payload is filtered through `tablesToSend` on the way OUT, since a privacy decision is either enforced in one place or hoped for in several, and `talksAutomatically(role)` replaced every `role === 'partner'` transport gate. Today the shopping list is the single area that merges between two people. Still open: setting up a child or a caregiver link at all.

### Open next step 27

27. **External data program: nine public-data lookup projects behind one Cloudflare Worker.** Written up 2026-09-14 into the [Project Tracker](https://app.notion.com/p/c9597dcb8a1d4cc5bc34ef87a4a097df) as nine Deferred rows plus the Decision row [External lookups: three privacy shapes, one Worker](https://app.notion.com/p/3db53652f272816d8051f1d335574853). Nothing is built. This is accepted scope rather than a loose idea, so read those rows, which name each project's sources. The rule settled first, which every outside request follows: (1) a keyed lookup, a barcode or product name in and a label out, routed through the `inside-story-site` Worker off a D1 snapshot with the edge cache in front, so only the key leaves the phone; (2) anything keyed by condition, pre-fetched by the Worker for all 19 on a schedule and downloaded as a whole bundle, so a device never makes a per-condition request; (3) anything keyed by location, coarsened to a rounded coordinate or a city and never the precise fix, stated in-product and opt-in. Agreed order: recalls and weather first, then supplement and OTC barcode work together. Cost baseline is Workers Paid at $5/month from the day the first lookup ships. One product rule carried over: when a refresh brings a newer record for something already saved, the app offers it on next open and never silently replaces what the person confirmed.

29. **What grows on the freed tab screens, designed 2026-09-24 and not built.** 1.0.51.1 emptied every tab screen body so a person's use of the app could show there over time (Phase 2 of the 2026-08-21 header growth plan, whose Phase 1 registry is `lib/achievementCriteria.ts`). The design conversation that followed is in `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md` under "The reward design for the freed tab screens", `lib/achievementCriteria.ts`'s header comment carries the constraints, and the Project Tracker holds three rows: the settled Decision [Reward design for the freed tab screens](https://app.notion.com/p/3e553652f27281c383fcc4155c7b6e79), the Open Feature [Fill out the achievement criteria registry](https://app.notion.com/p/3e553652f272812f8dc1d61fda97a455), and the Open Decision [distinct things or repetitions](https://app.notion.com/p/3e553652f272812883e1ed771d38adb4). **One decision governs the rest: what grows is made out of the person's records rather than awarded for them**, because a record cannot be taken away, needs no praise language, and simply stops growing through a gap instead of wilting. That rules out streaks, levels, points and percentages outright, since `scripts/test_keeping_up.js` bans praise ("well done", "good job", "keep it up") as squarely as blame and a blank period draws as a gap rather than a zero. Four more constraints hold: **no animation** (the AnimatedSky came out 2026-08-17 for battery drain, and this would be mounted behind nine tabs), it stays reachable when a tab's background is Off or a photo somebody added, **elapsed time earns part of it** so light-but-long use still shows, and nothing ever regresses. **Decoration is not the motivator**: the honest one is proximity to an answer ("Pattern Finder needs four more meals logged alongside a symptom before it can say anything about dairy"), which is a statement about what the analysis requires and never about the person. **Two things gate any build.** The open question is whether growth counts DISTINCT things or repetitions (recommendation: variety plus elapsed time, since variety is the gut-healing goal and repetition rewards grinding). And the registry is lopsided: Food 17, Schedules 6, Insights 5, Signals 1, Garden 1, with **Home, Trends, Reports and Life at none at all**, Life being the sharpest gap since it is the second audience's tab.

Ancestry is optional and in the person's words, with GEDCOM in and out so the tree outlives the app. Passing it down re-expresses every relationship from the child's side ("my mother" becomes "your grandmother"). A relative's health is theirs too, so it is off the allowlist between people by default. The Family list on Conditions stays the meal-planning household, linked to the tree, never a second copy. **Contacts** becomes the one record of a person that `emergency_contacts`, the family tree, resume references, Appointments and Keeping in touch all link to, imported one ticked contact at a time with every field for reaching someone, and never overwritten quietly on re-import. Phone import needs `expo-contacts` and `READ_CONTACTS`, so it is rebuild-gated; Outlook import needs `Contacts.Read` added to `ONEDRIVE_SCOPES` and a second consent, and on the desktop app (no Microsoft sign-in) it is a .vcf or .csv file, which ships OTA everywhere. ## App Lock follow-ups and App Lock on the desktop (2026-10-03, 1.0.60.6 and 1.0.60.7)

Appended 2026-10-06 when that session closed. **1.0.60.6 (aefe7f07)** covered follow-ups 1 to 4 on the phone:
- **Turn Off App Lock.** `startTurningOff` sets phase `decrypting`, and `runUnlockMigration` exports through `sqlcipher_export` and checks every table before the encrypted file goes. `keepLockOn` is the way back when that fails.
- **Waits after wrong passcodes.** Five tries are free, then waits of 30 s, 1 min, 5 min and 15 min (`checkPasscode`, `wrongTryWaitMs`). Nothing is ever wiped.
- **Reminders name only their kind** unless Profile says Full Detail (`lib/lockedReminderText.ts`).
- **Asks again before records leave** for backup, restore, sync, PDF, print, CSV, the emergency PDF, connect and pair (`lib/freshAuth.ts`, `components/FreshAuthHost.tsx`, `components/ConfirmItsYou.tsx`).
- Checked by `scripts/test_app_lock_followups.js`.

**1.0.60.7 (a73261d7)** brought App Lock to the desktop.

How the records are kept:
- `node:sqlite` has no cipher, so the records are sealed as `<db>.sealed`: `ISSEAL01` (8 bytes), a 12-byte nonce, a 16-byte tag, then AES-256-GCM ciphertext (`desktop/sealedDb.js`).
- `desktop/sqlite.js` unlocks by deserializing the file into memory. It writes the file back sealed 500 ms after a change (waiting while a transaction is open) and on close, then zero-fills the key.
- While locked, a read is refused with "Inside Story is locked." rather than making an empty plain file.
- `main.js` calls `sqlite.closeSealed()` on `did-start-loading` and `render-process-gone`, because a page reload is how the app locks and restarts.
- Turning the lock on or off copies the file, compares the row count of every table, and only then deletes the source (`planSealMove`: copy, finish, no-database).
- A fresh install with no database gets an empty sealed file, so a plain file never appears.

Windows Hello and the app side:
- `desktop/hello.js` calls WinRT `KeyCredentialManager` through PowerShell 5.1 with `-EncodedCommand`; stdin mishandled multi-line blocks.
- The app's Hello key signs a fixed random challenge. RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 gives the same signature every time, and SHA-256 of a label plus that signature opens an AES-GCM copy of the data key, stored in `BIOMETRIC_ITEM` through the DPAPI secrets shim.
- `lib/desktop/expoSqliteShim.ts` turns `PRAGMA key = "x'<hex>'"` into the bridge's `unlock`.
- `lib/appLockDevice.ts` has an `isDesktopApp()` branch for every move, with `finishLockingOn` and `finishTurningOff` shared by phone and desktop.
- `lib/appLockWords.ts` words the screens as computer and Windows Hello, and the screenshots row is hidden on the desktop.

Checks, limits and what is still open:
- Checked by `scripts/test_desktop_seal.js` (111 checks). The new modules are listed in `electron-builder.yml`'s `files:`.
- Limits: Mac is passcode only, the window is not blanked in the task switcher, and screenshots cannot be blocked.
- Followed by fixes in other sessions (1.0.60.10: scrypt 2^12 rewrap and a Lock Now button; 1.0.60.15: desktop setup URL fix and Bring My Records Back). Tony confirmed App Lock working on the PC on 2026-10-03.

## How this document works

This file is the standing brief a new session reads automatically: current status, product direction, architecture decisions, and standing rules. It is deliberately kept small so it fits comfortably in context.

**The full history lives elsewhere and is not auto-loaded:**

- **`docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE.md`** holds the complete, unmodified 2.05M-char original of this file: the dated build journal from 2026-07-18 through 2026-08-19, plus the long-form reasoning behind every decision summarized here. Read or grep it when you need the history behind a specific decision. It is not loaded into context automatically.
- **`docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`** holds everything removed from this file on 2026-09-14 and on 2026-09-23: the 2026-09-13 status snapshot, two 2026-09-05 snapshots (a short entry and a full one, the latter merged on 2026-09-24 out of two near-duplicate copies that had been stored side by side), a superseded revision of the brief sections below, and, under "Removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-23" and "Removed from CLAUDE.md on 2026-09-26", the verbatim build accounts, bug histories and enumerations condensed out of the sections below across three passes that day. Where a section below says the full account is in the archive, that is where it is. Also not loaded into context automatically.
- **[Lifestead Notion hub](https://app.notion.com/p/3a853652f2728144bde2d78ead5227ea)** has day-by-day decisions and an explicit built-vs-planned reconciliation. New findings get written up there first.
- **[App Development Log](https://app.notion.com/p/3a853652f27281ccb21aeaa9bec8c2ae)** has the full reasoning per change.
- **`unified-database/README.md`** is the authoritative, dated history for that track (1,700+ lines, newest entry at top).

**Keep this file lean.** This file is a brief, not a log. When a session finishes work, put the long-form account in the Notion log and, if a dated snapshot is worth keeping, APPEND it to `docs/CLAUDE-ARCHIVE-2026-09-14.md`. Never add a Status snapshot section to this file, and never prepend a new copy of this file above the old one. That append-only habit grew this file to 2.05M characters in August 2026 and to 1.6M characters again by 2026-09-14, stopping Claude Code from responding both times. If this file exceeds ~2,000 lines or ~100 KB, stop and archive before doing anything else.

## What this app is

**Lifestead** since 2026-10-09 (1.0.65.4), tagline "Everything in your life has a place." It was called Inside Story until then, a name chosen after ruling out Aurelia, Chrysalis, Monarch, Second Nature, Food Sense, FoodFlex, and Backstory; the reasons for leaving it are in `docs/name-knockout-2026-10-08.md`. Every name was changed to Lifestead on 2026-10-10 except identifiers that hold records or reach a device: the Android package and iOS bundle `com.insidestoryapp.app`, the EAS project, the `hashimotosapp` scheme, the insidestoryapp.com domains and the Worker, the database file `inside_story.db`, secure-store and crypto labels, notification ids, the app://inside-story origin, and the sync, session and Tell Claude note file names in the shared folder. The GitHub repository is `Antonio-BandeRock/Lifestead` since 2026-10-10 (it was `Inside-Story`, and GitHub forwards the old address), and the dev folder is `C:\Dev\lifestead-app` once `C:\Dev\rename-to-lifestead.cmd` has been run. The GitHub CLI, `gh`, is installed; it needs `gh auth login` done once by Tony in a browser before it can act. "A life's Inside Story" and The Inside Story section of Your Story keep the phrase as an idea, not as the app's name. **No text a person reads says Inside Story, messages included** (direct instruction, 2026-10-12): a message built around one of the kept file names passes it through `lib/fileInWords.ts`, and `node scripts/audit_old_name.js` must stay at 0.

**Never describe this as a Hashimoto's app, or even only an autoimmune-conditions app.** The creator's framing: "everything has an inside story… This app started to help with Hashimoto's, then decided to help with 18 other conditions, then has grown from there to include basically everything in life revolving around a person." Describe it as an everything-about-a-person's-life app that started with, and runs deepest on, food and autoimmune health. Garden, budget, family, soil microbiome, and the body are all in scope.

**Scope, stated directly:** "this is no longer just focused on Hashimoto's, it is focused on all 19 both individually and if a person has multiple of them combined." Every one of the 18 non-Hashimoto's conditions is a standing target for the same depth, not a lesser tier. Combined-condition (polyautoimmunity) management is its own named scope item, not yet built as a first-class destination.

**Who it is for, past the 19 conditions.** Direct statement, 2026-09-16: "I would like for this app to not just be viewed as being for the 19 conditions. The Autism and ADHD additions don’t much have anything to do with food at all, but the app itself is the thing that will help people who do have those neurodivergent traits to cope with daily living and all of the details that do need to be kept track of and reminding them of and making sure they have a way to keep all of those things from being on their minds. That in itself, I think will be a boon for them."

So there is a second audience with as strong a claim on this app as the health one: someone who needs an outside place to hold the details of daily living, so those details stop taking up room in their head. ADHD and autism are the named cases, and the need is wider than that (anyone recovering, grieving, caregiving, or simply carrying too much). For that person the point of the app is not the food scoring at all. It is Life, Schedules, reminders, and capture. The health depth is there when they want it, not the price of entry.

Two things follow, and they change what gets built:

1. **A feature that serves only the 19 conditions is a narrower feature than one that also serves this.** When both are within reach for the same effort, build both.
2. **The way in must not require a condition.** Onboarding, the Free tier, and the store description all still lead with health conditions. Someone who came for help running their day should recognize the app as theirs on the first screen. Not built, and a named gap.

**Never frame this as diet or nutrition treating ADHD or autism.** Nutrition supports them; it does not treat them, which is the line the Digest’s own ADHD entries already take. The daily-living support stands on its own and needs no food claim attached to it.

### The core purpose (read before any scope trade-off)

Help someone with an autoimmune condition relearn how and what to eat, and understand, personally and for their own body, how food affects them. Meal building, shopping lists, and scheduling are scaffolding that make daily use sustainable enough to generate that understanding. They are not the point. **When in doubt about priority, favor whatever helps someone discover and act on their own personal food-effect patterns over convenience features.**

Gut and microbiome healing is an explicit goal, not a side effect. The app is meant to actively help repair gut health, not just avoid trigger foods.

**Food first, and a supplement only for what food cannot supply.** Direct statement, 2026-09-22: "the goal is to modify how a person eats so with their food they are receiving an optimal amount of every one of them and not have to take any supplements, but to also make sure that you do take the ones you cannot receive from your food because of whatever reason, such as being vegan, or alergic, etc." A target reached by food and the same target reached by a capsule are two different outcomes, so everywhere the app shows a nutrient amount it says which one happened, and neither half of that is advice to stop taking anything.
